LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. away.headline: Patriots injury analysis after Bears loss in Week 7
away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. The first injury report of the week will be published on Wednesday afternoon, and give more information about the current state of the team. Kickoff between the Patriots and Dolphins at Miami’s Hard Rock Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.

away.headline: Chicago Bears' unique way of honoring the late Mike Ditka adds a new element to Week 7's game against New England Patriots
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field for their first home game since legendary coach Mike Ditka passed away, and fans in attendance against the New England Patriots are in for something special. The Hall of Fame tight end and former head coach died on Oct. 9 at the age of 86 . Ditka remains one of the most important figures in Bears history and in NFL history , and the organization is going all out to celebrate him in front of a primetime audience at Soldier Field. The Chicago Bears host the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football in one of the most anticipated games of the 2026 NFL season, and it doubles as the team’s first home game since the passing of legendary former Bears coach Mike Ditka. Ditka led Chicago to a Super Bowl title over the Patriots following the 1985 season, which makes this matchup a fitting stage to honor him. Chicago Bears plan a stadium-wide tribute to honor Mike Ditka The Bears already honored Ditka with No. 89 jersey patches last week on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. Chicago will continue wearing the for the rest of the season in his honor. Now that the team is back home, fans get a chance to be a part of the tribute. The Bears will hold a stadium-wide mustache giveaway on Thursday night, a nod to the iconic mustache Ditka always wore. On top of that, the first 10,000 fans getting into Soldier Field will receive a Bears knit headband inspired by Ditka’s trademark sweater vest. The tribute extends to the field itself. Fans will see a commemorative Ditka stencil on the Soldier Field grass, and there will be a moment of silence held before the national anthem. The Bears also have an on-field recognition planned, along with other moments honoring the legendary coach, including a special tribute, throughout the game. It’s a great way to honor Ditka while getting the fans involved in what’s already shaping up to be a special night. Patriots-Bears has become the hottest ticket in the NFL The storylines on the field alone would make this a must-watch game. Bears head coach Ben Johnson and his Patriots counterpart were both in the running for Coach of the Year last season. Meanwhile, two of the most dynamic young quarterbacks in the league go head-to-head when Caleb Williams and Drake Maye take the field. Fans clearly noticed. ESPN’s Field Yates noted earlier in the day that the Patriots-Bears game has become the most expensive ticket for any NFL game so far this year, with a get-in price of $702 on TickPick. So, needless to say, the atmosphere at Soldier Field is set to be packed and electric. For the fans paying that kind of price to get in the building, the Ditka tribute adds even more meaning to the night. home.headline: Patriots injury analysis after Bears loss in Week 7
home.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. Barmore walked off the field and with the Patriots playing no more defensive snaps did not get an opportunity to reenter the game. What this means for the Patriots While the injuries to both Kevin Byard and Christian Barmore could have been potentially concerning, it appears neither will be a long-term issue. Byard returned to the game, while head coach Mike Vrabel said about Barmore on Monday that “he’ll be fine.” Him and Barmore both being present at practice on Monday is concrete proof of that. For the Patriots, especially considering that they were on a short week, this is definitive good news. The team, after all, had at least lost some starters or key reserves to injury in almost every game this season so far. Now heading into a Week 8 contest against the Miami Dolphins off a mini-bye, they seemingly are trending in the right direction again. No major injuries were added on Thursday, while the team is getting healthier — as evidenced by the fact that guard Ben Brown (knee) also was back on the practice fields on Monday. The first injury report of the week will be published on Wednesday afternoon, and give more information about the current state of the team. Kickoff between the Patriots and Dolphins at Miami’s Hard Rock Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday.

home.headline: Will Kyle Monangai Return in Week 8? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears RB
home.blurb: Will Kyle Monangai Return in Week 8? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears RB Skip to main content SI.COM Monangai has actually been listed with toe and thumb injuries on the team's injury report since Week 5, but the toe issue has been the one keeping him out. Will Kyle Monangai return in Week 8? If he is able to get in any practice participation, it would be a huge step toward his return, as Monangai has not practiced once since coming down with his toe injury. When is Kyle Monangai Coming Back? Injury Update, Return Timeline Ahead of Week 8 The Chicago Bears have not had one half of their electric running back duo for the past three contests as Kyle Monangai continues to work his way back from injury. As we turn the page to Week 8, the hope is that Monangai will be able to make it back into the lineup, and there's reasons for optimism that he will be able to be. Here's what we know about Monangai ahead of the Week 8 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks on Monday night. Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai (25) reacts after a play against the New York Jets during the second quarter at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We do not have full confirmation that Monangai will play this week, but there's a few reasons to believe he will. We do not have full confirmation that Monangai will play this week, but there's a few reasons to believe he will. For starters, the Bears never placed Monangai on injured reserve, which is a clear indication they do not expect him to miss more than three games. Had Chicago placed him on IR, he would've been forced to miss four contests. Now that he has missed three games, there's a good chance the Bears running back will be ready to go. Along with revealing the Bears wouldn't place Monangai on IR, head coach Ben Johnson noted that the Bears rusher is progressing through his rehab back on Oct. 16. "It wasn't something we felt required an IR stint. It remains a week-to-week situation, but as far as I know, he's continuing to trend in the right direction," Johnson said . Another thing working in Monangai's favor is the Bears have extra rest this week. Chicago played its Week 7 game against the New England Patriots last Thursday night and won't take the field for the next game versus the Seahawks until Monday night. We'll have a better idea of where Monangai stands on Thursday, when the Bears drop their first injury report of the week. Roschon Johnson has been filling in for Monangai behind D'Andre Swift, and he had a bad game in Week 5 followed by a good game the following week, although he did lose a fumble that almost proved very costly. In Week 7, Johnson was barely involved, as Swift carried the load for Chicago with 26 touches to Johnson's two. Swift could be in for another big workload in Week 8 if Monangai returns and the Bears decide to limit his snaps in his first game back. home.headline: Chicago Bears' unique way of honoring the late Mike Ditka adds a new element to Week 7's game against New England Patriots
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field for their first home game since legendary coach Mike Ditka passed away, and fans in attendance against the New England Patriots are in for something special. The Hall of Fame tight end and former head coach died on Oct. 9 at the age of 86 . Ditka remains one of the most important figures in Bears history and in NFL history , and the organization is going all out to celebrate him in front of a primetime audience at Soldier Field. The Chicago Bears host the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football in one of the most anticipated games of the 2026 NFL season, and it doubles as the team’s first home game since the passing of legendary former Bears coach Mike Ditka. Ditka led Chicago to a Super Bowl title over the Patriots following the 1985 season, which makes this matchup a fitting stage to honor him. Chicago Bears plan a stadium-wide tribute to honor Mike Ditka The Bears already honored Ditka with No. 89 jersey patches last week on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. Chicago will continue wearing the for the rest of the season in his honor. Now that the team is back home, fans get a chance to be a part of the tribute. The Bears will hold a stadium-wide mustache giveaway on Thursday night, a nod to the iconic mustache Ditka always wore. On top of that, the first 10,000 fans getting into Soldier Field will receive a Bears knit headband inspired by Ditka’s trademark sweater vest. The tribute extends to the field itself. Fans will see a commemorative Ditka stencil on the Soldier Field grass, and there will be a moment of silence held before the national anthem. The Bears also have an on-field recognition planned, along with other moments honoring the legendary coach, including a special tribute, throughout the game. It’s a great way to honor Ditka while getting the fans involved in what’s already shaping up to be a special night. Patriots-Bears has become the hottest ticket in the NFL The storylines on the field alone would make this a must-watch game. Bears head coach Ben Johnson and his Patriots counterpart were both in the running for Coach of the Year last season. Meanwhile, two of the most dynamic young quarterbacks in the league go head-to-head when Caleb Williams and Drake Maye take the field. Fans clearly noticed. ESPN’s Field Yates noted earlier in the day that the Patriots-Bears game has become the most expensive ticket for any NFL game so far this year, with a get-in price of $702 on TickPick. So, needless to say, the atmosphere at Soldier Field is set to be packed and electric. For the fans paying that kind of price to get in the building, the Ditka tribute adds even more meaning to the night. Home crowd will be a major factor for Chicago The timing of this home game couldn’t be much better for Chicago. Here are our picks Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 31-17 This is a unpredictable game that could go either way without considering both teams' records. However, the New Orleans Saints' defense does not inspire confidence in stopping the Pittsburgh Steelers. Aaron Rodgers remains a solid quarterback at age 42, passing for nearly 1,500 yards with 12 touchdowns and five interceptions. Allowing 377 passing yards to Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy does not bode well for New Orleans. While the win over the New York Giants was notable, New York lacked a running back like Jaylen Warren to keep the Saints' defense honest. Warren has rushed for 460 yards on 84 carries, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt. His ability to gain yards after contact, identify lanes and contribute to the passing game gives Pittsburgh multiple offensive options. That creates a difficult matchup for New Orleans. The Saints allows 138 rushing yards per game, ranking 30th in the NFL, while Pittsburgh averages 99.2 rushing yards per game, ranking 20th. Despite Pittsburgh's modest team average, Warren's efficiency indicates the Steelers can exploit the Saints' rushing defense. For New Orleans to win, its offense must perform consistently throughout the game. The Steelers present a tougher matchup than the Giants and have their starting quarterback available. While Tyler Shough offers New Orleans its primary offensive spark, the offensive line must protect him against T.J. Watt, who excels at pressuring quarterbacks. Steelers 31 Saints 17 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 28-21 After getting their collective tails chewed out by the team owner a week and a half ago, the Saints put together a better effort in a win at the New York Football Giants last weekend. Now, after a week in the mother country (at least the one for New Orleans and its state), players and coaches alike are saying this is the best week of practice the team has had all season. Meanwhile, a visibly exhausted Aaron Rodgers spoke to the media on Thursday, the day his Pittsburgh Steelers arrived in Paris, worried about jet lag and getting to France so late in the week. True, the Steelers are favored, and rightfully so with a flip-flop record of 4-2 compared to the Saints. But this game seems more and more like a home game for New Orleans fans as even Harry's New York Bar "changed its name" for one day to celebrate the team and its fans. Harry's New York Bar becomes Harry's New Orleans Bar for one day. | Harry's New York Bar Instagram There is, of course, the immediate retort that home field advantage is a myth for this program. And if you thought that, you'd be correct, as the Saints haven't won at home since December 21, 2025. However, most of us didn't see the turnaround this team did in a week. However, the AFC North has four teams over .500, putting the Steelers in a spot where they can't afford many losses early in the season. Meanwhile, New Orleans is off to a 2-4 start, snapping a three-game skid in Week 6 when they beat the New York Giants. Shough and company have performed pretty well on offense, but New Orleans is sitting in third place in the division at just 2-4 through the first six weeks. This is technically a home game for the Saints, and they're set as underdogs against Rodgers and the Steelers. This line opened up 2.5 points (Pittsburgh favored), and it has since moved to three. The Steelers have a top-10 defense in EPA/Play, while the Saints are a bottom-10 unit and sit dead last in the league in EPA/Rush. For example, they scored 30 points with 411 yards in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and put up 34 points in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. It's possible that Pittsburgh comes out a bit sluggish against the Saints in Paris after arriving later in the week, but the formula is there for the black and gold to have another huge performance. New Orleans' defense is currently tied with the Arizona Cardinals for the most points allowed per game (29.7) while also giving up the fourth-most yards per contest (377.7). The Saints have struggled to consistently get after the quarterback too, as their 33.2 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) is the fourth-worst in the NFL despite having 15 sacks. The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh Forces Two Turnovers The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league. At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11. The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5). New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to. Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Win by Two Scores Steelers Win by Two Scores Pittsburgh is short-handed along the interior of its defensive line with Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) joining Derrick Harmon (foot) on the reserve/injured list. The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game . Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week. Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team. The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2. That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers. After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2. away.headline: Saints vs. Steelers: Final Week 7 injury report updates key starters
away.blurb: Week 7 starts out with the 2-4 New Orleans Saints and the 4-2 Pittsburgh Steelers facing off in the first ever NFL game played in Paris, France. The Saints left for France immediately after their game at the New York Giants last Sunday. Pittsburgh elected a different approach, arriving in Paris on a red-eye flight early Friday morning. Here is the final injury report for both teams. For the first time this season, the Saints have not ruled out a player on a Friday before a game. Right guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and defensive lineman Nathan Shepherd (illness) are both listed as questionable. Shepherd did not participate at all in team activities on Friday. He has missed the last two games with an illness. Ruiz left last week's victory over the Giants late in the first half with a knee injury and did not return. He had missed practice all of this week until returning in limited duties on Friday. Rookie fourth round choice Jeremiah Wright replaced Ruiz in the lineup against the Giants and played well. Rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, the team's first round pick, made the trip to Paris but has not been activated off injured reserve. With the Saints on a bye next week, Tyson could return in Week 9. New Orleans does expect linebacker and defensive captain Kaden Elliss to play against the Steelers. Elliss has missed the last three games with a calf injury but returned to practice this week and was a full participant on Friday. Kicker Daniel Carlson also returned to the team, flying into France later in the week. Carlson and his wife are expecting a baby, explaining his late arrival to France. Running back Alvin Kamara, dealing with a back injury, was limited in practice all week but does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek (calf) and cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) are both listed as out for the Steelers. Running back Rico Dowdle is dealing with a knee injury and saw only limited practice duty all week. He's listed as questionable. Also listed as questionable is safety DeShon Elliott, dealing with a knee injury but a full practice participant most of the week. Taken off the injury report for the Steelers is pass rusher Alex Highsmith, who was limited most of this week with a groin injury but returned to full duties on Friday. away.blurb: The former Defensive Player of the Year didn’t practice on Wednesday for a rest designation. But, then he was limited in practice on Thursday because of a calf injury. This is a new injury to the public. There was some good defensive news coming out of the Steelers’ injury report, though. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey was limited on Thursday after not practicing the day prior with a wrist injury, so that was improvement. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was also limited with a groin issue, the same designation as Wednesday. It seems like a new star player is being added to the injury report each week. Thursday’s injury report included a surprising name, one that Steelers fans wish wasn’t on the list: edge rusher T.J. Watt. It’s unclear when or how Watt suffered the calf injury. But, now there’s a possibility, even if just a slight one, that Watt could miss Sunday’s game in Paris against the New Orleans Saints . Watt being absent for a game is always a loss for the Steelers. He can always make big and important plays for his team. Through six games this season, Watt’s recorded 4.5 sacks (tied for eighth in the league), 15 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery. Veteran tackle Cameron Heyward didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday for rest designations, but he should be good to go come Sunday. Safety DeShon Elliott recorded his second-straight full practice on Thursday, meaning he’ll likely play on Sunday. It would mark Elliott’s first game since last October after he suffered an MCL sprain, hyperextended knee and a hamstring injury. Atlanta is searching for its first home win of the season, but San Francisco presents a major test for a team still trying to find consistency on both sides of the ball. Despite the 49ers dealing with injuries, the Falcons will need a complete performance to pull off the upset. Here is how our staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Garrett Chapman (3-3) The Falcons are winless at home this season, and they will need to pass a difficult test Sunday to change that trend. The undefeated 49ers have established themselves as one of the league’s top teams, and Atlanta enters the matchup with defensive holes to fill and an offense still searching for consistency. If Michael Penix Jr. can stay clean in the pocket, the Falcons will have a legitimate chance to compete. However, slowing down George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey will be especially difficult without linebacker Divine Deablo. San Francisco’s offensive weapons could prove too much for Atlanta’s defense, leading to another disappointing home result for the Falcons. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 17 Scott Kennedy (3-3): At first glance, the betting line makes this matchup appear favorable for Atlanta. A 6-0 San Francisco team might be expected to be a bigger favorite, but the 49ers’ extensive injury concerns could be keeping the matchup closer than anticipated. The Falcons have enough talent to beat any team when they put everything together. The problem is finding that consistency against quality opponents. Atlanta must figure out how to handle opposing pressure, or the 49ers could overwhelm Penix with aggressive blitz packages. San Francisco is vulnerable because of its injuries, giving Atlanta a puncher’s chance. However, until the Falcons prove they can consistently perform against strong competition, picking them to pull off an upset remains difficult. Prediction : 49ers 31, Falcons 23 Darius Hayes (3-3): After Bears fans took over Mercedes-Benz Stadium last week, I expect another takeover from 49ers fans on Sunday. Atlanta should deliver a much better performance, but I still have concerns about whether the offense can do enough to secure a victory. San Francisco’s injuries will have an impact, but Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey will ultimately be too much for Atlanta’s defense. Meanwhile, the 49ers’ pass rush could make life difficult for Penix, particularly if the Falcons struggle to protect their young quarterback. I expect Atlanta to keep the game competitive and give its home crowd something to cheer about. However, until the Falcons demonstrate they can finish against a quality opponent, I cannot pick them to get over the hump. San Francisco escapes with a narrow victory, leaving Atlanta with another frustrating home loss. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 24 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-3) The 49ers are currently the best team in football in my opinion which makes this a tough matchup for the Falcons. This would be a lopsided matchup if the 49ers were healthy, but that’s not the case. The 49ers have been led by arguably the best passing attack in the league, but they’ll be without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Stopping Georgie Kittle and McCaffrey will still be a tall order, however. The Falcons offense matches up well against the 49ers defense on paper, especially given that Nick Bosa will be out. The key will be can the Falcons o-line deal with all of the twists and stunts that the 49ers will throw at them, and can they keep Fred Warner from taking over the game. I have the 49ers winning, but I think the Falcons will keep it close. Prediction: 49ers 27, Falcons 20 Gerald Thomas, III (3-3) These are the kind of games the Falcons win. The skid continues. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Brewers rout Rays in Game 3 Cowboys clobber Eagles Valkyries beat Dream in Game 5 Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or NFL predictions: Can Falcons take advantage of 49ers injuries? SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 19: Mac Jones #10 of the San Francisco 49ers is rushed by Zach Harrison #96 of the Atlanta Falcons during the third quarter in the game at Levi's Stadium on October 19, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images Kevin Knight Sat, October 24, 2026 at 1:17 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Atlanta Falcons are sitting at 2-4 after a disappointing two-week stretch. Atlanta desperately needed to find a win over the past few weeks, instead dropping a game to the Tyler Huntley-led Ravens and (understandably) to the finally healthy Bears. The Falcons didn't play terribly in either game, but in both, it was too little too late from Atlanta's offense. TNow the team enters the unenviable situation of needing a win against an undefeated 49ers team that has pretty consistently looked like one of the NFL's best units despite a growing injury list. That lengthy injury list, along with some rest and off-field advantages, could help the Falcons pull off the unlikely upset in Week 7. The bettors seem to think so as well, as Atlanta is just a 2.5-point home underdog according to FanDuel. Falcons vs 49ers predictions On paper, the 49ers are clearly the superior team. San Francisco is one of only a handful of teams who are top-10 in both offense and defense, and one of only two who are top-5 in both categories. To put it simply, there aren't any obvious glaring weaknesses on this team—except their long injury list, which is only growing heading into Week 7. That's something the Falcons will have to take advantage of to come away with an improbable victory. The 49ers offense struggled mightily once Mike Evans, who Falcons fans know quite well, left the game against the Commanders in Week 6. Washington was close to mounting a comeback, but was ultimately unsuccessful due to their own issues. Evans, along with Deebo Samuel, have both been declared out for Week 7. Those are major losses, and when combined with San Francisco's other injuries at the position, could be too much for the passing game to overcome. Atlanta is dealing with their own injury problems, particularly on defense. Starting slot corner Billy Bowman and linebacker Divine Deablo are both out, and three other cornerbacks are questionable. It does sound like A.J. Terrell and C.J. Henderson are likely to play on Sunday, but a new injury (and questionable designation) for rookie Avieon Terrell throw a wrench into things. Veteran Mike Hughes, who has struggled mightily this season, will be on track to start again unless those players are cleared. Already down Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr., Atlanta is looking at questionable designations for Za'Darius Smith and Samson Ebukam on the edge. Standout interior pass rusher Gervon Dexter Sr. also picked up a questionable tag heading into the weekend. Atlanta is perilously thin on the edge and can't afford any more losses here. If Atlanta can get most of these players in the game on Sunday, they may have a significant health advantage over San Francisco. History is also unkind to West Coast teams traveling to play in the 1pm timeslot on the East Coast, and the 49ers are working off a rest disadvantage after just playing on Monday Night Football. Health and extra rest could be critical to the Falcons pulling off the upset. That'll, plus Atlanta figuring out how to deal with blitz pressure and opposing defenses crowding the line of scrimmage. Michael Penix Jr. has been outstanding when kept clean this season, but he's absolutely cratered when faced with pressure. Part of the issue is that Atlanta has been allowing the fastest time to pressure in the NFL by quite a wide margin, giving Penix little time to react. Hopefully that's been a major point of emphasis in practice this week. I'm not confident in Atlanta's ability to take down a superior opponent, especially coming off the past two weeks. So I'm going to say that the 49ers should win this game. However, Atlanta's potential health advantage along with the extra rest and the West Coast-East Coast factors could combine to give the Falcons a real shot in this one. Plus, Evan would be remiss if I didn't mention the RED HELMET ENERGY. It's uncanny, but the Falcons typically play great in this uniform. Will they pull it off? That's the question I don't feel confident answering.

away.headline: Five Fixes the 49ers Must Focus on During the Bye Week
away.blurb: The 49ers have won six games despite injuries across the roster, particularly at wide receiver, where their top five options were unavailable against Atlanta. Shanahan offered encouraging updates Monday, starting with Christian McCaffrey , who briefly left Sunday's game with a hamstring injury. The strain is considered mild, and Shanahan is optimistic he'll be available against Las Vegas. Nick Bosa also has a chance to return after missing five consecutive games with a calf injury. His presence would be especially welcome as the 49ers prepare for their remaining 10 regular-season games. The offense could also get a significant boost. Mike Evans , Deebo Samuel , and Demarcus Robinson are among the players who could return following the bye, potentially giving Brock Purdy a much more experienced receiving group. Defensively, C.J. West , Marques Sigle , and Upton Stout could also be available, while linebackers Luke Gifford and Garret Wallow remain possibilities. De'Zhaun Stribling remains on track for a possible December return, while Sam Okuayinonu isn't expected until January. During the bye, the 49ers can evaluate available kickers while continuing to work with Piñeiro. His field-goal accuracy gives them reason to believe he can improve, but the repeated extra-point misses are becoming difficult to overlook. Bosa's return would help, but San Francisco also needs to prepare for teams that try to neutralize its pass rush regardless of who's on the field. The defensive line remains an area worth evaluating. Bosa's return should improve the pass rush, but the Falcons game also demonstrated how quickly an opponent can limit its effectiveness. Lynch also has to consider what the team already has. Several players could return after the bye, and those additions will affect both the roster and the need for outside help. Trades also carry costs in draft picks, salary cap commitments, and available roster spots. With the deadline approaching, Lynch can use the bye to evaluate whether an addition would justify those costs. picks.headline: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Aside from their records, these two teams are oddly similar. Their defenses tend to carry them and keep games close, while their offenses tend to struggle, particularly early on in games. Cleveland is well-equipped to win those slog-style games, but will they slip up in the Music City? Here are our predictions for Week 7. Anthony Moeglin It's a Cleveland Browns party on Broadway this weekend in Nashville, Tennessee. The Browns come into this game as the favorite for the first time all season and probably the last time all season. They have a chance to get to 5-2 on the year and stay in first place. They get it done on Sunday against the Titans. Spencer German Last week was a barometer game to assess how the Browns stack up with a legitimate Super Bowl contender, even if that contender was missing it's MVP quarterback. But this week, in some ways is an even bigger test of whether or not the Browns are as good as their record says they are. Great teams beat the teams they're supposed to beat and Cleveland does just that on Sunday to improve to 5-2. Yes, it is basically a Pick 'Em heading into Sunday. Cleveland is -1.5 favorites in this one, and I see a 20-3 winner for Cleveland where the defense shuts it down, and the offense gets it going a little bit on Sunday. This one is basically a Pick 'em with the Browns being listed as favorites for the first time this season (and on the road nonetheless) by 1.5. I think that means they easily cover, with a 17-9 victory. A 300-yard day for Deshaun Watson I'm 0-6 on bold predictions this year, so let's go way out there. Deshaun Watson throws for 300 yards on Sunday for the first time in his Cleveland Browns career. It would be a monumental day down in Tennessee if this bold prediction comes true. The Browns score 7 on their opening drive Despite Todd Monken's presence as an elite offensive mind, the Browns have yet to score on an opening drive this season. They've also only scored six points in the first quarter this season. In a game featuring two struggling offenses, the one that gets off to a better start could be in the driver's seat for a win. Finally, Cleveland gets to play with a lead.

away.blurb: Why Is Dillon Gabriel’s Return Creating A Roster Problem For The Cleveland Browns? | NFL | NDTV US Sports NDTV Dark / Light mode Oct 27,2026 06:11 PM IST Why Is Dillon Gabriel’s Return Creating A Roster Problem For The Cleveland Browns? facebook twitter WhatsApp Settings Change Font Size A A arrow-down reddit snapchat twitter facebook comments email printer search bell top-nav reddit-fill snapchat-fill twitter-fill facebook-fill share whatsapp-fill bookmark arrow-rgt arrow-next arrow-up refresh close link cog star book zap cricket football tennis formula-1 badminton hockey golf boxing ndtv-n check left-arrow right-arrow Sports Home US Sports NFL Why Is Dillon Gabriels Return Creating A Roster Problem For The Cleveland Browns Related Articles Dillon Gabriel Return Tests The Cleveland Browns' Roster Math Head coach Todd Monken did not rule out the crowded look. Asked whether keeping four was realistic, he said, “Sure it's possible. Hell, it's possible we'll pick one more up and have five.” It sounds like a joke, and partly it is. Still, it tells us the staff has not locked in a plan. The Browns announced they have activated QB Dillon Gabriel (back) from injured reserve. Cleveland now has four quarterbacks on the active roster with the return of Gabriel. https://t.co/YDBMYRNN1a हिंदी Featured Links New Zealand vs India NFL Trade Targets: Minnesota Vikings Eye Two Indianapolis Colts Stars To Boost Their Unbeaten Run Could Dante Moore Skip The 2027 NFL Draft After His Season-Ending Injury? Russell Wilson’s Heartfelt Message To Ciara Reveals What Matters Most As They Prepare For Baby No. Five The Cleveland Browns are 5-2 and leading the AFC North, but activating Dillon Gabriel has created a crowded quarterback room behind Deshaun Watson. With Shedeur Sanders and Taylen Green also on the roster, a trade or a cut may be coming soon. Updated: October 26, 2026, 10:27 PM EDT Winning cures plenty of problems in the NFL, but it cannot create extra roster spots. The Cleveland Browns learned that Monday when quarterback Dillon Gabriel came off injured reserve and the team had to cut tight end Carsen Ryan to fit him. Deshaun Watson still runs the offense, and the Browns sit at 5-2 atop the AFC North. Yet the room behind him now holds Shedeur Sanders, Gabriel and rookie Taylen Green. Four passers for a single job is a luxury no true contender can afford for long, and the Browns must pick a direction soon. Cutting Carsen Ryan shows how seriously the Browns took this move. Ryan was a 2026 draft pick, and teams rarely let rookies go unless the squeeze leaves no clean option. A fourth quarterback rarely helps on special teams, so he takes a spot that a blocker or defender could fill. That is the real cost. Stability at the top makes that patience affordable.

Brian Flores' aggressive unit ranks among the stingiest in the league against both the pass and the run (just 259.8 YPG allowed overall), and that spells trouble for an Indianapolis Colts team that's lost 11 of its past 13 contests and had three costly turnovers last weekend. Minnesota's bye week has also cleaned up the injury report, with T.J. picks.blurb: Colts vs. Vikings | Predictions & Picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Brewers rout Rays in Game 3 Cowboys clobber Eagles Valkyries beat Dream in Game 5 Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or Colts vs. Vikings | Predictions & Picks (Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images) Jake Arthur Sun, October 25, 2026 at 1:12 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There's usually a clear path to victory for the Indianapolis Colts, even when they aren't playing well, regardless of the opponent. However, they do not match up well with the Minnesota Vikings this Sunday. The Indianapolis Colts (2-4) will attempt to ground themselves on Sunday as they travel to Minneapolis to face the host Minnesota Vikings (5-0) before their season truly spirals out of control. The Colts' 2026 campaign is at a crossroads. After consecutive losses, including an embarrassing finish last week to the previously winless Tennessee Titans , the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard . Will that move spark the Colts and help them turn the tide, or will the team retreat into its shell? Trade rumors and thoughts of a slide are once again surrounding the Colts. This game could be a back-breaker unless they can avoid it. Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Vikings 23, Colts 13 "I'd often like to lead with the optimistic take on the matchup with a clear advantage the Colts have over their opponent, but I'm not sure there is one this week. Minnesota's defense blitzes far more than any other team, which is something the Colts' offense struggles against. The Colts can usually run the ball, but opponents are running against Minnesota less than anyone else because of the defensive fronts the Vikings present. The Vikings' offense isn't doing well despite having Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson, but they've had a week to figure out what to do, coming off their bye. "The Colts would often have the edge on special teams and penalties, but Minnesota's special teams are just as good as Indy's, if not better, and the Colts and Vikings are tied for being the second-least-penalized teams in the NFL. No Tyler Warren or Sauce Gardner for the Colts, and Minnesota doesn't have a soul on the injury report. The Vikings have the clear advantages in this one." Jake on the season: 2-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Vikings 19, Colts 9 "The Colts limp into Minnesota coming off of their most embarrassing loss since 2024. They are without two of their best players in Warren and Gardner, while the 5-0 Vikings are looking healthy coming out of their bye week. "The Vikings boast the top defense in football, while the Colts' offense can't get out of their own way. This seems to be a recipe for disaster, with very little room for the Colts to make up this disadvantage. This should be an ugly kickers duel, with the Vikings coming out on top." Zach on the season: 4-2 The Colts take on the Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS .

picks.headline: Vikings Close to Being Unanimous Pick to Defeat Colts on Sunday
picks.blurb: Vikings Close to Being Unanimous Pick to Defeat Colts on Sunday - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Brewers rout Rays in Game 3 Cowboys clobber Eagles Valkyries beat Dream in Game 5 Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or Vikings Close to Being Unanimous Pick to Defeat Colts on Sunday (Stephen Lew-Imagn Images) Aiden Checketts Fri, October 23, 2026 at 7:32 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings are ready to get back on the field on Sunday as they were on a bye in Week 6 and are hoping to continue their strong start to the season to improve from 5-0 to 6-0 if they can defeat the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7 . Speaking of the Vikings chances against the Colts, the NFL analysts and experts have spoken and based on the results, Minnesota appears to be a strong favorite on Sunday. Recently, Minnesota Vikings contributor Sam Thiel collected the predictions from all sorts of experts, and the results of these predictions clearly favor the Vikings over the Colts. To start Pete Prisco of CBS Sports and Bill Bender and Vinne Iyer of Sporting News all picked Minnesota. Then Thiel noted that NFL.com was 5 for 5 picking the Vikings for Sunday. Looking at more picks, Bleacher Reports was 6 for 7 in favor of the Vikings, ESPN was 11 for 11 picking Minnesota, The MMQB went 8 for 8 when it came to their experts selecting the Vikings to come out on top, and lastly, the Athletic had 7 of 8 analysts pick Minnesota as well. So, when seeing the overwhelming majority of the pick from the NFL analysts for the Vikings to win once again, it does seem pretty clear that Minnesota has a decisive advantage according to the majority of analysts. Now, one thing that the Vikings do need to be way of as Thiel notes is that Minnesota has lost in their last two opportunities which suggests that there could be some trouble for the Vikings in this game if they are not careful. However, it is important to note that Minnesota is at home and will have the support of a very passionate home crowd. With all that said, this game overall does favor the Vikings when looking at the record as well as how these two teams match up. Currently, Minnesota sits at 5-0 while Indianapolis sits at 2-4 and is actually coming off a loss to one of the worst teams in the NFL in the form of the Tennessee Titans who actually earned their first win by defeating the Colts. When it comes how these teams match up, the Vikings do need their offense, to play much better, but ultimately this game will come down to how the Minnesota defense and defensive coordinator Brian Flores are able to do against Colts running back Jonathan Taylor who is one of the best backs in the entire league. For the season, Taylor has 122 carries for 492 yards, seven touchdowns, 30 first downs, one fumble and one fumble lost while averaging 4.0 yards per carry 82.0 yards per game. On the Vikings side, they are allowing 86.6 rushing yards per game which is No. 5 in the league and thus far they have only allowed one player to reach 100 rushing yards which shows their to stop the run on a consistent basis. So, heading into Sunday, it will be interesting to see if the Vikings can shut down Taylor and the Colts, because if Minnesota does win that matchup they will likely improve to 6-0 and prove the experts the right to continue the strong start.

At 2-4 on the season and having just fired GM Chris Ballard, the Colts ' season feels as if it's on the verge of spiraling. The next few weeks will likely play a pivotal role in determining how Indianapolis approaches the Nov. 10 trade deadline. As far as this week's game goes, the Vikings will present a unique challenge with their aggressive and blitz-heavy approach on defense under defensive coordinator Brian Flores. The Vikings' passing game, meanwhile, features Justin Jefferson. Can the Colts come away with a crucial win? Here is what the experts are predicting. A clean sweep -- and not in favor of the Colts. All eight ESPN analysts are picking the Vikings to win. Pro Football Talk Mike Florio is picking the Vikings to win by multiple scores, 30-17. Kyler Murray also seemed to settle in more in Week 5 against the Saints, posting his best completion percentage (80%) and passer rating (109.6) as a Viking. Now, he's coming off a bye to face a bottom-10 defense." Pete Prisco is picking the Vikings as well, although he does believe it will be close. Vikings win, 21-18. "The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. The Indianapolis Colts today elevated cornerback Kenneth Harris and linebacker Germaine Pratt to the active roster from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. The team also released punter Thomas Morstead from the practice squad. Harris , 6-0, 192 pounds, was elevated in Week 1 vs. Baltimore and registered one solo tackle. He was signed to the team's practice squad on August 31, 2026. Harris participated in training camp with the Colts after originally signing with the team as a free agent on August 26, 2026. home.headline: Vikings get positive injury update on RB Aaron Jones: report
home.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for the Miami Dolphins Against New York Jets Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The 0-5 Miami Dolphins take on the 2-4 New York Jets in Miami’s first divisional game of the 2026 season. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. New York has lost four of its last five games, and they have failed to score 20 points four times during that stretch. The circumstances favor New York, but this rivalry has a way of making things complicated, especially when one team is desperate for victory. With that in mind, it's time to make some bold predictions for Sunday's matchup, including a few outcomes that might not be on everyone's radar. Geno Smith throws two touchdown passes, including one to Garrett Wilson Smith threw for 252 yards and a touchdown against New England, but his first interception of the season proved costly. He needs to respond with a cleaner performance against Miami, particularly if the Jets want to establish some rhythm early rather than waiting until the second half to find their passing game. Prediction: Smith throws two touchdown passes without an interception, with Wilson catching one of them. Getting New York's top receiver involved earlier would give the offense a better chance to dictate the pace rather than play catch-up. Omar Cooper Jr. scores in consecutive games Cooper's return from injury against the Patriots was one of the brightest developments of the afternoon. He caught six passes for 103 yards and his first career touchdown, immediately showing the potential to become a dependable option alongside Wilson. Now comes the challenge of following that performance with another productive outing. Prediction: Cooper winds up on the other end of the other Geno Smith TD pass as he finds the end zone for the second straight week. Here's where he begins giving Smith another reliable target as the Jets look to build continuity in the passing game. David Bailey records two more sacks Bailey recorded three sacks against Cleveland in Week 5, then went without one against New England. That swing illustrates how difficult it can be for a pass rusher to produce consistently, but Miami presents an opportunity to bounce back. Prediction: Bailey records two sacks against the Dolphins , helping set the tone for a defense looking to rediscover its disruptive form. The Jets force three turnovers and limit the Dolphins to 275 yards or fewer The Jets need to pressure Miami's quarterback into hurried decisions and capitalize when he puts the ball in danger. Creating turnovers would give New York additional possessions and help compensate for an offense that has struggled to sustain drives. Prediction: New York forces at least two turnovers, creating opportunities for the offense to score without having to manufacture long drives on every possession. The extra possessions also help keep the Dolphins offense off the field. Jets break the 20-point barrier and win by seven The Jets have struggled to score consistently this season, but Sunday's matchup offers an opportunity to change that narrative. New York has the playmakers to produce more than 20 points, particularly if Geno Smith establishes an early connection with Garrett Wilson and Omar Cooper Jr. That's where all predictions for this one begin. New York will continue building on positives established against New England. The defense also has a chance to create favorable field position by forcing turnovers and putting pressure on Miami's quarterback. If the Jets capitalize on those opportunities instead of settling for field goals or wasting possessions, they can generate enough offense to control the game. Prediction: Jets 24, Dolphins 17. New York finally breaks the 20-point barrier, gets a more complete performance from its offense, and earns a seven-point victory at MetLife Stadium to improve to 3-4. That gives them momentum as they enter a Week 8 home date with the Las Vegas Raiders . This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: Jets vs. Dolphins: Bold predictions for Week 7

away.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. away.blurb: Long snapper Tucker Addington (shoulder), edge Robert Beal Jr. (hamstring), wide receiver Caleb Douglas (ankle), tight end Will Kacmarek (hamstring), safety Kyle Louis (knee), and running back Jaylen Wright (foot) have all remained limited through two practices. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley stated that they would see how both Douglas and Louis would practice to determine if they could return in Week 7. Douglas may be a bit farther along than Louis, but the receiver has been limited for two straight days. If he remains limited on Friday, that may point to him not being able to play. However, being limited does not rule one out either. Additionally, Louis has also remained limited due to a knee injury. The case might be that he will remain out to heal up more and be ready to play in Week 8 instead. The Dolphins barely opened up the 21-day practice window for Louis, meaning that he will have up to 21 days to officially return and be ready to play. home.headline: Jets finally get some good Breece Hall injury news on Week 7 practice report
home.blurb: One of the biggest is the Breece Hall quad injury, which has kept him out for multiple weeks now. However, the Jets got some good news before Week 7 on Hall's injury. As the Jets announced in their Thursday Week 7 practice injury report, the star running back was finally upgraded at practice, as he was no longer a DNP but instead listed as a "limited" participant. The Jets shared their Week 7 injury report for their game against the Miami Dolphins . Right in the middle of the injury report, Hall was seen with his quad injury as going from a "DNP" on Wednesday to a "LP" on Thursday. What that means is that, for the first time in a while, Hall got in a limited practice, which bodes well for his chances of suiting up on Sunday against the AFC East rival Dolphins. He isn't guaranteed to play this week, but getting in a limited practice, going from not participating on Wednesday to a limited participant on Thursday, is a sign that he's trending in the right direction. Jets fans should keep a very close eye on the Friday injury report, because if Hall's a full participant, he's as good as playing. But even another limited participation would indicate his work Thursday went well, and he'd have a chance to go in Week 7. picks.blurb: Our Buccaneers vs. Panthers Score Predictions Are In Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers face a grim outlook for the rest of the season if they fall to 1-6 on the year. They can prevent that by defeating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, but it won't be easy to win their first division matchup. The Bucs will have Baker Mayfield back in the fold after a three-game absence, but will that be enough to get a win? Our staff goes over our predictions for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 21 It’s been tough sledding for the Bucs, but they might just have a chance to turn things around. Division play begins this week against the Panthers, and all signs point towards Baker Mayfield being back. While I do believe things will look better, I still think the offense is way off from being able to match Carolina’s offense, which will put up points. I think the Bucs will have a chance to win the game on the final drive, but ultimately fall short once again. James Hill, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 20 Mayfield's return is spoiled by the Panthers in this one. I simply think that Carolina is the better-coached team right now and that Mayfield may be slow to start back up after returning from his thumb injury. Collin Haalboom, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 17 The Buccaneers have played so poorly this season that they’re already on the verge of switching their primary focus from postseason contention to the top pick in next year’s NFL Draft. Considering we’re not even halfway through the season, I’d consider this season to be a full-scale nightmare for any Bucs fan. So, am I picking the Buccaneers to bounce back and take down the NFC South-leading Panthers in Carolina, you ask? No. I most certainly am not. Logan Robinson, Founder: Panthers 28, Bucs 23 The Panthers head into the game with the top passing attack in the league, and Bryce Young is playing at a high caliber. The Bucs and Todd Bowles have done a fair job of defending these types of offenses this season. My biggest concern is the offense for Tampa Bay. It’s quite obvious Zac Robinson’s offense doesn’t have an identity and even with Baker Mayfield coming back, I just don’t see it changing much. They’ll have to begin proving me wrong before I pick them to win games. Also, a reminder — the Cowboys are a bad football team. River Wells, Editor: Panthers 28, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay's defense will be tested by a Panthers offense that playcaller Brad Idzik has unlocked this season. Bryce Young is stretching the football down the field in a dominant way, so expect the Panthers to score points. Don't expect the Bucs to do much on offense in return. Zac Robinson's offense has been scattershot this whole season, and while Mayfield should play better than Jalon Daniels, he'll be playing with an injured thumb after a year where he didn't start off so hot anyway. Bucs have to be able to run the ball on Carolina — if they can't, they have no chance of winning. Consensus: Panthers 5, Bucs 0 The Buccaneers still haven't given us a reason to pick them to win a football game. They're 1-5 as it stands, and every BucsGameday staff member thinks they'll be 1-6 whenever they wake up in the morning. away.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
away.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball. away.headline: Only Two NFL Experts Are Picking the Buccaneers to Upset the Panthers in Charlotte
away.blurb: Baker Mayfield is set to return in Charlotte wearing a glove the Tampa Bay Rays helped build , and the national crowd still isn’t sold on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Nearly every major outlet picking Sunday’s NFC South opener at Bank of America Stadium has the Carolina Panthers winning. Parr worried about Mayfield returning “without the services of WR1 Emeka Egbuka,” and Egbuka was ruled out Friday, one of the new holes on offense Mayfield walks back into. Parr also flagged that the Bucs “have the second-lowest QB pressure rate (29.6%) despite blitzing at the third-highest clip (43.8%), per Next Gen Stats.” By our count, Tampa Bay gets two of 32 straight-up picks across NFL.com, ESPN, CBS Sports, USA Today, Sports Illustrated and Pro Football Talk. The Bucs are 3-point underdogs even after Todd Bowles said Friday, “It looked good for him, so it looks like he’s ready to go,” per the team’s website . None of the scores point to a rout. Every predicted score below lands within five points, which fits a team that has played 12 straight one-score games .
