home.headline: Jaelan Phillips is out, but his injury isn’t the only puzzle Panthers have to solve
home.blurb: Canales soon clarified that Phillips will be out for Sunday’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers: “I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of.” With Phillips officially out — it’s unclear if he’ll be ready by the Panthers’ Thursday Night Football game against the Packers in Week 8 — the Panthers are missing more than a run-of-the-mill defensive starter. The 27-year-old who the Panthers signed to a four-year, $120 million contract this free agency has lived up to his billing as a premier pass rusher; he has 2.5 sacks through five games but has also added 18 total pressures in the pass rush — 24th among all edge rushers , according to Pro Football Focus. Phillips has also been stout against the run and a vocal leader his teammates praise. What’s also a result of Phillips being out? The absence of Phillips comes at the same time as reserve outside linebacker and special teams ace Thomas Incoom is also “week to week” with a calf injury. Incoom exited the Eagles in the first half and didn’t return, and as a result the Panthers needed to do a whole bunch of roster magic to fill his role on special teams. In each of the four special teams units Incoom contributes on — kick return, kick coverage, punt return, punt coverage — the Panthers needed to replace him with four different players, Canales said. Canales was asked if the Panthers will elevate anyone from the practice squad with Phillips and Incoom out, and he indicated that Nick Hampton would. The interior offensive lineman was placed on the team’s injured reserve before the season began due to a hamstring injury and is now waiting for his 21-day practice window to be activated. When asked Wednesday, Canales was vague about Christensen’s situation: “We’re just evaluating it, and you gotta figure out roster spots as well,” before adding that he has faith in the team’s current slate of IOLs. If Christensen were to return, that limits their flexibility to use the injured reserve. It’s also worth noting the Panthers have already waived someone off the injured reserve with an injury settlement — Claudin Cherelus a few weeks ago — to avoid further limitations. It’s possible, perhaps likely, that once Cherelus gets healthy, he’d re-sign with the Panthers, rejoining the squad without forcing the team to use one of its eight precious IR-elevation moves. home.headline: Panthers have lost stunning amount of projected workload to injuries in 2026
home.blurb: By my estimates, Carolina has lost 24 percent of its projected workload to injury (edge rusher Nic Scourton and receiver Chris Brazzell were lost to season-ending injuries in camp, while cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are also out). That is the second-highest figure in the league. Given the mounting injuries they've been dealt here in 2026, the Carolina Panthers may want to consider adding a witch doctor to their staff. The pain began early on in training camp, with the season-ending knee tears to rookie wideout Chris Brazzell II and starting outside linebacker Nic Scourton. Since then, the Panthers have had a dozen other significant setbacks—and even with the recent returns of several players, they're still hurting bad. Right tackle Taylor Moton is the latest to fall. After just returning to the lineup in Week 6 from being sidelined for months due to blood clots , the longtime hog molly went down with a broken fibula in Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . He, per head coach Dave Canales, will obviously miss quite a bit of time. And at this point, according to Mike Sando at The Athletic , the Panthers have lost nearly one quarter of their projected workload to injuries. Only one team has had it worse. As it happens, that team is the Green Bay Packers, who will be hosting the Panthers on Thursday night to begin Week 8. Despite a barrage of bad luck, Green Bay is in the thick of an extremely competitive NFC North race. Meanwhile, Carolina's lead in the NFC South is looking perilously thin, especially after the Atlanta Falcons upset the previously-undefeated San Francisco 49ers in Week 7. home.headline: Panthers inactives vs. Buccaneers: Another starter down as injuries keep piling up
home.blurb: Phillips is obviously the big one here. He's been starting on the outside, and with him out, Princely Umanmielen is expected to get the start opposite Patrick Jones II. Carolina also elevated Nick Hampton from the practice squad Saturday to give the Panthers another option on the edge. That's a group I'm going to be watching against Baker Mayfield. He's back after missing three games with a thumb injury, but his return shouldn't change what Carolina expects from this game . The last thing the Panthers want is to let him get comfortable early. Robert Rochell was elevated from the practice squad again this week, so Carolina is still having to make things work in the secondary without its two starters. Now Phillips is out, too, which takes another starter away from a defense that's actually been playing some pretty good football lately. The rookie tackle is active after missing last week's game with a knee injury. He practiced fully all week but was still listed as questionable heading into Sunday. With Stone Forsythe inactive, having Freeling back gives Carolina another option behind Rasheed Walker and Taylor Moton. Sam Hecht is also inactive, so the Panthers will have Torricelli Simpkins III and Corey Bullock available behind Austin Corbett at center. Both can snap the ball if something happens and Carolina has to shuffle the offensive line again. The Panthers haven't had much luck staying healthy this season, and Sunday against Tampa Bay isn't going to be any different. Carolina already knew it would be without Jaelan Phillips after he aggravated his hamstring against Philadelphia. Thomas Incoom injured his calf in the same game and was placed on injured reserve Saturday, and the Panthers are still waiting on starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson to get back. It seems like every week Carolina gets somebody back and loses somebody else. Panthers inactives against Tampa Bay The Panthers announced seven inactive players before Sunday's 1 p.m. kickoff. QB Haynes King (emergency third quarterback) Incoom is a little different. He hasn't played much on defense, but he's been a big part of Carolina's special teams. The Panthers activated Bam Martin-Scott from injured reserve Saturday, and that's where he should be able to help right away. Carolina is still trying to piece things together The Panthers have already spent the last few weeks without Horn and Jackson after both starting cornerbacks went down in Week 3. Horn is working his way back from a significant quad injury, while Jackson had surgery for a groin injury. Both remain on injured reserve, but Dave Canales had some encouraging news Friday. He said Horn is ahead of some of the normal timelines for his injury, while Jackson has also started picking up his speed as he works his way back. That's good news for later. It doesn't help much Sunday. Carolina held Philadelphia to 222 total yards and just 35 on the ground last week . The Panthers have now held two straight opponents under 50

home.headline: Only Two NFL Experts Are Picking the Buccaneers to Upset the Panthers in Charlotte
home.blurb: Baker Mayfield is set to return in Charlotte wearing a glove the Tampa Bay Rays helped build , and the national crowd still isn’t sold on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Nearly every major outlet picking Sunday’s NFC South opener at Bank of America Stadium has the Carolina Panthers winning. Parr worried about Mayfield returning “without the services of WR1 Emeka Egbuka,” and Egbuka was ruled out Friday, one of the new holes on offense Mayfield walks back into. Parr also flagged that the Bucs “have the second-lowest QB pressure rate (29.6%) despite blitzing at the third-highest clip (43.8%), per Next Gen Stats.” By our count, Tampa Bay gets two of 32 straight-up picks across NFL.com, ESPN, CBS Sports, USA Today, Sports Illustrated and Pro Football Talk. The Bucs are 3-point underdogs even after Todd Bowles said Friday, “It looked good for him, so it looks like he’s ready to go,” per the team’s website . None of the scores point to a rout. Every predicted score below lands within five points, which fits a team that has played 12 straight one-score games . NFL.com: Panthers 4, Buccaneers 1 Jeremy Bergman is the lone NFL.com analyst taking Tampa Bay, calling a 24-20 upset. Brooke Cersosimo (24-22), Gennaro Filice (22-17), Bobby Kownack (24-20) and Dan Parr (23-21) all went with Carolina. David Walker is the exception. He has 14 pressures and four sacks on 57 pass-rush snaps, and his 82.6 overall grade ranks seventh among 115 edge defenders, according to PFF . He has earned an every-down role , and our bold predictions for Sunday have him sacking Bryce Young twice. CBS Sports and Pro Football Talk see a field goal or less Pete Prisco of CBS Sports has Carolina winning 24-23. “The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big,” he wrote, before adding, “It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around.” Young is averaging 309.8 passing yards per game with 11 touchdown passes and two interceptions. His 85.2 overall grade ranks sixth of 35 quarterbacks, per PFF , and he set a franchise touchdown mark through five games. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk went 20-17 Carolina: “The Bucs end up in yet another one-score game.” ESPN, USA Today and SI leave Dan Graziano alone Graziano is the only one of ESPN’s 11 experts picking Tampa Bay, according to the Bucs’ roundup . Pamela Maldonado and Eric Moody both have Carolina winning 24-20 in ESPN’s Week 7 predictions , and the Football Power Index gives Carolina a 56.6% win probability. All six USA Today staffers took Carolina, per the same roundup, and Sports Illustrated’s eight staffers did the same. Mayfield’s protection could decide which side is right. The Bucs are on pace to allow 62 sacks , and Carolina linebacker Bobby Okereke has 10 pressures, fourth among linebackers, with a 77.5 pass-rush grade, per PFF . Carolina is without edge rusher Jaelan Phillips (hamstring). More on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers Who Replaces Emeka Egbuka for Baker Mayfield? Answering 5 Questions Buccaneers Fans Are

With Lamar Jackson officially ruled out due to an ankle injury, my Bengals vs. Ravens prediction backs Cincinnati to capitalize in today's pivotal AFC North showdown. Fresh off their bye week, the Bengals head to M&T Bank Stadium as 1.5-point road favorites, with kickoff set for 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Baltimore's quarterback situation opens the door for some intriguing trading opportunities, and my latest NFL picks target value across the moneyline, anytime touchdown, and completions markets this afternoon. TOP Pick Bengals vs Ravens prediction today: Bengals moneyline Editor's note: Jackson has now officially been ruled out and will miss his third straight game. Even though I gave them out at +2.5 earlier this week , I'm still willing to trade the Cincinnati Bengals 51% moneyline, up to 53% , against the Baltimore Ravens . Lamar Jackson has been limited in practice all week after missing the past two games, so there is no way he'll be 100% Sunday if he plays at all. An injured Lamar weakens Baltimore's offense , especially its ground game, because he's less likely to run, which is his biggest skill. Jackson averaged only 20.1 rushing yards per game when he returned from injury last season, and the Ravens missed the playoffs. Meanwhile, Cincinnati enters off a bye with a much cleaner injury situation . Since 2024, Baltimore is 1-5 against the spread (ATS) with a rest disadvantage and a -4.8 spread differential. For a straight-up pick on every game, see our NFL moneyline picks for Week 7 . Bengals vs Ravens combo This combo makes sense if Cincinnati turns the game into a Joe Burrow -controlled grind instead of asking its rushing attack to carry the offense. I want the Bengals living in manageable down-and-distance situations, stacking first downs, and forcing Baltimore to defend long possessions. That naturally gives Burrow more chances to pile up completions while increasing the odds that Ja'Marr Chase eventually finishes one of those drives in the end zone. The other side of the script matters, too. If Baltimore's offense is less explosive than usual, Cincinnati can stay patient and keep leaning on what Burrow does best. Give me Burrow moving the chains, Chase cashing in near the goal line, and the Bengals hanging around long enough to finish the job. Cincinnati may have to lean more heavily on Burrow's arm in this matchup. The Bengals rank 27th in yards per rush, while Baltimore is ninth in yards per rush allowed, making the passing game the cleaner path to points. And if Burrow is throwing near the goal line, Chase is obviously his first look. Chase has eight touchdowns in 10 career games against Baltimore and leads Cincinnati with four touchdown catches this season. Some receivers can be schemed out of games. Chase usually isn't one of them. For more touchdown props, see our NFL anytime touchdown picks for Week 7 . picks.headline: Final score predictions for Bengals vs. Ravens in Week 7
picks.blurb: Final score predictions for Bengals vs. Ravens in Week 7 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Power Rankings Brewers rout Rays in Game 3 Cowboys clobber Eagles Valkyries beat Dream in Game 5 Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or Final score predictions for Bengals vs. Ravens in Week 7 Chris Roling, Bengals Wire Sun, October 25, 2026 at 1:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads A Week 7 clash between the Cincinnati Bengals and Baltimore Ravens quickly turned from Trey Hendrickson revenge game narratives to all things Lamar Jackson. Hendrickson is the former Bengals player with weird things to say about the club , but Jackson is the star quarterback who was injured all week and ultimately ruled out . Jackson's absence doesn't guarantee the Bengals anything on the road, though. Tyler Huntley has been adequate in relief as the starter for the 4-2 Ravens, with Derrick Henry bruising his way to seven scores already and the defense steady under new head coach Jesse Minter. Some of the hesitation comes from the Bengals' side. Are they going to hit the ground running out of the bye? Joe Burrow's offense has eased off the sluggish under-center attempts already after struggles. Chase Brown struggling to get going, to the point Samaje Perine looks more effective, remains a question mark. Then there's the defense. The annual question around the Bengals still doesn't have a solid answer. Will pain points like Jordan Battle and the linebackers correct angle, tackling and other issues enough to prevent big plays? Bengals fans don't need to be told how dirty some backup quarterbacks have done the team over the years. All valid questions, especially on the road. But when it boils down to prediction time, two big things stick out: Health and Ja'Marr Chase. Things are so fresh in Cincinnati that they didn't even list a player on the final injury report. The Ravens are battered and missing a star quarterback. And Chase? He's torched the Ravens his entire career. He averages 7.5 catches for 120.4 yards over 10 games against the Ravens. Keep in mind, too, this is the exact reason the Bengals traded for Dexter Lawrence. Bully ball in the AFC North. He's dominant in the middle and the edge rushers are strong, creating a good-looking front against a backup quarterback, a formula that should prevent Henry from controlling the game. If the Bengals drop this opportunity against the Jackson-less Ravens, it's time to start asking some serious questions. But the Bengals' strengths align very well in a way that can hurt the hosts and help them move to 4-2 after the bye. away.blurb: Jackson has been absent in the last two games. After sustaining an injury in a Week 4 game against the Tennessee Titans, he has not played a single minute. He has now come out to speak against a report about his return. Rapoport has not issued a statement in regards to Jackson's comments. The player is still listed as questionable for the next game against the Cincinnati Bengals, and has talked about the situation. Lamar Jackson talks about potential return Jackson has been participating in limited practice sessions. While he is still listed as questionable, the quarterback is doing his best to recover. He talked about his injury situation in the press conference, and revealed that he does not know when he would return. He said , "I can't call it right now. I still [have] got a grace period, so we'll see, but hopefully. I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now." He added, "I don't have a number, but I don't feel like I have to be 100. If I can just be out there and tolerate the pain in my ankle, [then] that's it. If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play. But [if] I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, [then] I'm not helping [anybody]. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and be hit, that's not helping my team at all. That's just me. I feel like I'm being selfish, because it's about me at that point, for me to go out there and be hurt." away.headline: Report: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson ruled out for matchup with Bengals
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has reportedly been ruled out for the team's divisional rivalry game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday. #Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) has been downgraded to out for tomorrow’s game vs. the #Bengals . Lamar Jackson has been downgraded to out for Sunday’s game against the Bengals. Your Privacy Choices/(Opt-Out of Sale/Targeted Ads) According to NFL insiders that include NFL.com's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter, the three-time first-team All-Pro quarterback will remain sidelined this weekend as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. The 29-year-old suffered the injury in Week 4 during the Ravens' game against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before. During the Bengals' matchup with the Ravens, Cincinnati will be seeking to extend its record to 4-2, which is what all three of the other AFC North teams currently remain tied at going into Week 7. However, due to the early bye week, the Bengals currently sit at 3-2, putting them last in the division. away.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins returns from Kyle Hamilton's hit to catch TD
away.blurb: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins was injured during the third quarter of the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium but returned a short time later to catch Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow's second touchdown pass of the day. Higgins' arm and shoulder were observed on the sideline by team medical personnel after taking a huge hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton following a 10-yard catch on third down during the Bengals' second drive early in the second half. Higgins remained on the Bengals' bench after observation. He had a 19-yard catch during the Bengals' next possession, his third reception of the second half. He caught the TD from Burrow later in the same drive. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. Against the Jaguars, Higgins got up slowly after a 19-yard catch near the sideline from Burrow . Higgins got up, but then took a knee and required attention from team medical personnel. Higgins returned to the game later in the drive, and made a catch on his first play back in the game. He was not on the field for the Bengals' final drive of the game. Higgins had a game-high 10 catches for 140 receiving yards before the injury. He added a 17-yard catch, giving him a total of 157 receiving yards, second only to the 194-yard game he had against Baltimore in 2021. Higgins made a remarkable touchdown catch from quarterback Burrow late in the second quarter of the team's Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. It was among the most impressive NFL catches by Higgins . In March 2025, Higgins agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team. picks.headline: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction
picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants might have a winning record (3-2-1) right now and lead the NFC East. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. After a 0-4 start to the season, Houston got back on track with a 26-3 win in Tennessee, and then a 34-31 win over the Jaguars in London last week. Stuckey Sun, October 25, 2026 at 4:01 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants (3-2-1) and Houston Texans (2-4) will clash in Week 7 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Texans are 10.5-point favorites over the Giants on the spread, with the over/under set at 42.5 total points. Houston is a -500 moneyline favorite to win outright, while New York is a +385 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Giants vs Texans predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, October 25. Giants vs Texans pick: Texans -10.5 (-102) My Texans vs. Giants best bet is Houston to cover the spread (-10.5), with the best price currently available at FanDuel. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Giants vs Texans NFL Odds Giants vs Texans Spread : Giants +10.5 (-120), Texans -10.5 (-102) Giants vs Texans Total : over/under 42.5 (-115o / -105u) Giants vs Texans Moneyline : Giants +385, Texans -500 Giants vs Texans Preview for NFL Week 7 New York Giants Betting Preview: The Biggest Frauds in the NFL The Giants are currently sitting at 3-1-1, but let me be clear: this is the most fraudulent winning record in the National Football League. They could easily — and probably should — be 1-4. Look at New York's last four games since getting blown out by the Rams . The Giants beat the Titans (who fumbled at the goal line with a chance to win), beat the Cardinals (who threw a red-zone pick while driving for the win), they lost to the Saints 34-27 (who were blowing them out before a late surge), and they tied the Commanders (who went into turtle mode and forgot to kick a game-winning field goal). The Giants have played the easiest schedule in the league by a country mile — and to make matters worse, their offense is completely broken without Jaxson Dart. Since Dart went down, the Giants rank 31st in the NFL in rush success rate . Because they have absolutely no rushing attack, J.J. McCarthy — taking over for the benched Jameis Winston — is going to be forced to drop back and win this game with his arm. McCarthy has been miserable in his career when under pressure, currently sporting a -10% completion percentage over expectation (CPOE) when the pocket collapses. He hasn't has much time to learn the Giants' playbook, and the offense is already entirely disjointed. Houston Texans Betting Preview: Don't Be Fooled by the Poor Record The Texans are coming off a season-saving win and traveling back from the London game, but this does not qualify as a flat spot. There is a real sense of urgency for the Texans: they still need to win to keep their season alive after yet another slow start to the year. Unlike the Giants, Houston has played a top-10 schedule, facing the Bills , Bengals , Cowboys , Jaguars, Colts , and Titans. The Texans are also a couple of bad bounces away from having four or five wins. C.J. Stroud is playing at a very high level right now, looking like the rookie-year version of himself. He ranks in the top 10 in nearly every passing metric and sits third in the NFL in air yards , actively pushing the ball down the field. Most importantly, Stroud finally has his full complement of weapons. He operated without Nico Collins for a stretch, but now he has also Marvin Harrison Jr. and potentially Tank Dell returning. Defensively, this Texans unit is incredibly salty and built to shut down bad, inexperienced quarterbacks like J.J. McCarthy. Giants vs Texans Picks, Betting Analysis I view this game as an absolute burial of the Giants. You have a massive strength-of-schedule disparity between a battle-tested Texans squad and a fraudulent Giants team that has feasted on incompetent opponents making timely errors. Without a functional run game, J.J. McCarthy is going to drop back into a world of hurt against the Texans' pass rush. Meanwhile, C.J. Stroud should have a field day against a bad Giants secondary, potentially with some weather assistance. I expect a 30-13 blowout for the Texans so I'm laying the double digits with Houston. Can the Giants win? Of course. Will they? It's hard to predict. But here are four bold predictions for the Giants-Texans game Sunday. Cam Skattebo Will Score a Touchdown Skattebo hasn't found pay dirt since Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. But after his zero-touch performance in the Giants' 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints, Skattebo is poised to bounce back with J.J. McCarthy at quarterback and plodding veteran Najee Harris out of the picture. Skattebo scored in Jaxson Dart's only full game this season, and McCarthy boasts a Dart-style skill set. That should open up Skattebo to a bigger game. J.J. McCarthy Will Throw 2 Touchdowns and at Least 1 Interception The Giants need to stay balanced with Skattebo and reserve running back Tyrone Tracy Jr., but their best offensive matchup is McCarthy, Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers against the 27th-ranked Texans passing defense. So even though offensive coordinator Matt Nagy wants to have a run-first offense, McCarthy may end up pitching the ball around, especially in the second half. McCarthy has more interceptions (13) than touchdowns (12) in his NFL career, so he'll likely turn it over at least once. Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers Will Stay Hot The Giants passing offense broke out with Jameis Winston at quarterback, and McCarthy should be able to keep the momentum going against one of the league's worst pass defenses. McCarthy targeted Likely and Nabers quite a bit after he took over for Winston in the fourth quarter, since those two are matchup nightmares for the Texans. Houston also won't have safeties Jalen Pitre and Reed Blankenship, which means the deep middle of the field will be open. But McCarthy may also target rookie Malachi Fields, since both of Fields' receptions came with the 23-year-old quarterback last week. The Giants Will Be in the Game in the Fourth Quarter If you're betting, consider Giants +9.5, since they have been resilient and defying expectations all season. McCarthy nearly led them back from a 24-point fourth-quarter deficit against New Orleans. The Giants defense definitely will miss inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, who is out for the season with a chest injury. But their pass defense is fifth in the NFL, allowing only 190.2 passing yards per game. The Texans have allowed 14 sacks, which means the Giants could improve on their sack ranking, where they are tied for 31st in the league.

away.headline: Report: New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo avoided major injury
away.blurb: The extra rest should allow Skattebo to return healthy to the backfield as New York aims to maintain its divisional edge. News Sports Business Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals GIANTS Report: New York Giants RB Cam Skattebo avoided major injury Dan Benton Giants Wire Oct. 26, 2026, 10:50 a.m. ET New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo should avoid significant injury after feeling something in his hamstring on a 42-yard overtime run that helped secure a 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans on Sunday. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported on Monday that all indications are the second-year back should be OK, a rare positive for a Giants team that often has injured reserve (IR) candidates after games, particularly with a bye this weekend. After the Week 7 win, Skattebo told ESPN’s Dan Graziano he did not intend to slide on the play that set up Devin Singletary’s game-winning 30-yard touchdown. He felt something in his hamstring and knew the Giants were in field-goal range, so he went down at the Houston 30. He noted the bye week’s timing was fortunate. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reported that Skattebo avoided straining the muscle. The carry was the longest of Skattebo’s career and highlighted a bounce-back outing in which he rushed 17 times for a career-high 124 yards and a touchdown. It followed a week in which he received zero carries against the New Orleans Saints after an overtime fumble versus the Washington Commanders in Week 5. The Giants improved to 4-2-1, leading the NFC East, and will have the bye before traveling to Philadelphia on November 8. We may earn a commission when you buy through links on this page. away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that "without a doubt" it isn't easy to no longer have a starting role. "Whenever you're used to something, you've had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don't get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it's tough, but I think it's just about staying present," McFadden said. "This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. A lot of gratitude to be healthy and just to be able to play again, and I think that's what I found most throughout these past six weeks is just, just finding gratitude in whatever situation I'm in." The Giants designated cornerback Paulson Adebo to return this week, and it looks like he could be activated before Sunday's game. With starting cornerback Greg Newsome II still in concussion protocol and ruled out, there could be immediate snaps for Adebo vs. the Texans. Meanwhile, the Arizona Cardinals may be 2-4, but they're coming off a huge divisional victory over the Los Angeles Rams. The Cardinals are feeling it right now, and they're at home — but we know how Broncos Country travels, especially in the desert. At 4-2, the Broncos can't afford a slip-up — not if they want to keep pace with the Kansas City Chiefs in the division, and make their Week 8 rematch at Mile High a potential chance to get back to the top of the division, depending on what happens this Sunday with the Seattle Seahawks. That's me looking past the Cardinals a little bit. The Broncos won't be doing that. Sean Payton knows how to keep a team's focus on whichever game and opponent is up next, and that's the Cardinals. How will this one shake out? Let's go around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff see Sunday's action unfolding in Glendale, AZ. Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 4-2 : Getting Bo Nix back in the flow of things has become like a quest for the Holy Grail. All the internal tinkering on Nix might not be as important as facing a Cardinals team the Broncos should beat. While most eyes will be focused on how Nix performs, it's returning rookie running back Jonah Coleman who steals the limelight with two scores. Pick : Broncos 31, Cardinals 21 Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 4-2 : The Broncos' coaches and players are buzzing about a Nix breakout game. Looking at the Cardinals' 31st-ranked scoring defense — a unit allowing 350.5 yards per game — this is about as golden a get-right opportunity Nix could hope for. Courtland Sutton said , "At some point, the tide's going to turn" for Nix and this offense, and it happens at State Farm Stadium on Sunday. Nix passes for three touchdowns and 280 yards, while the Broncos romp in the desert. Pick : Broncos 27, Cardinals 17 Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-2 : Only speaking for myself, the Broncos haven’t yet earned the benefit of the doubt. Not yet. But if there’s any way to earn that — and any day to have a get-right game — it’s Sunday against the Cardinals. This goes for the offense more so than the defense, which has been fantastic of late. If not now for Nix, then when? Go out there and dominate, and those “confidence issues” will miraculously disappear. I foresee a better showing, though maybe not quite the 2018 Kick Your A** blowout. This is an inferior opponent who, quite frankly, the Broncos should handily dispatch. “Should.” Pick : Broncos 30, Cardinals 16 Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 4-2 : The Broncos' offense has been the source of much consternation. Is Nix hurt? Has the game passed Sean Payton by? Luckily, the Cardinals appear to be a get-right game. It's the NFL; there is no such thing as a guaranteed victory, but I expect the Broncos' defense and special teams, as well as continuity across the organization, to be felt in Arizona. I don't think the offense looks great... and even if it does, it's just one game, and the broader sample size should hold more weight in the total evaluation. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Broncos -4.5 (-110) Cardinals +4.5 (-110) Broncos: -230 Cardinals: +190 43.5 (Over -115/Under -105) This line has held steady since it opened , as the Broncos are still favored on the road by 4.5 points despite Arizona’s win over the Rams in Week 6. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The Cardinals are ninth in success rate and 15th in EPA/Play on offense, yet they’ve still scored 21 or fewer points in three of their six games. I expect Brissett to have a much tougher time against a Denver pass defense that – without Pat Surtain II – dominated Seattle and Los Angeles in back-to-back weeks. On the other side of the ball, how can anyone bet on Denver to put up points? The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. Kickoff is set for 4:05 p.m. ET from State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Ariz. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Broncos are 4.5-point favorites on the spread (Broncos -4.5), with the over/under set at 43.5 (-115o / -105u). Denver is a -230 favorite on the moneyline while Arizona is a +190 underdog. Let's get into my Broncos vs Cardinals predictions for Sunday, October, 25. Broncos vs Cardinals Odds, Lines Broncos vs Cardinals Moneyline: Broncos -230, Cardinals +190 Broncos vs Cardinals Total: 43.5 Broncos vs Cardinals Spread: Broncos -4.5 (-108), Broncos +4.5 (-112) Broncos vs Cardinals Preview Broncos Preview The Broncos are sitting at 4-2, but they are undeniably one of the luckiest teams in the NFL right now. All four of their victories have come by one possession, and their two losses were absolute blowouts. The Broncos easily could have lost to the Seahawks , who doubled them up in total yardage. Denver barely survived a completely broken Chargers team on the road, and needed big comeback efforts against both the Rams and the Jaguars . Bo Nix has been terrible all season. I saw a great stat on X recently: Bo Nix is five letters long, which is basically the same length as his average depth of target (aDOT) — the absolute lowest mark in the NFL. He simply refuses to push the ball downfield. Defensively, Denver is dealing with cluster injuries. The Broncos are likely going to be without both Patrick Surtain and Talanoa Hufanga , completely gutting the back end of their secondary. This could also be a look-ahead spot with the Chiefs on deck. Cardinals Preview The Cardinals are coming off a big win over the Rams, which our Evan Abrams noted was the biggest upset of the season so far with Arizona entering that game as a 12.5-point underdog. Of course, that means we're not buying a bad Cardinals team at the bottom of the market. Still, their offense is capable of exploiting a battered Denver secondary. Marvin Harrison Jr. may be out of the fold, but the Cardinals still have viable weapons in Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, and a reborn Kendrick Bourne. Yes, Arizona's defense isn't very good and consistently gives up points, but it has shown the ability to stay frisky in games and match opponents score for score. With Denver's defense missing its top playmakers in the secondary, Jacoby Brissett should find plenty of open windows. Broncos vs Cardinals Moneyline Pick This is simply me wanting to fade Bo Nix. I am going to force Nix to prove he can actually push the ball down the field and win a game by margin on the road, especially in a potential flat spot with Kansas City looming on deck for the Broncos. Denver has been scraping by against bad teams with improbable late-game variance, and that luck is bound to run out. Give me the Cardinals to win this game outright. away.blurb: Coleman was designated to return from injured reserve on Wednesday after missing the last four games. He still must be formally activated to the 53-man roster but is fully expected to play against the Cardinals. Coleman's return is especially helpful this week considering third-string RB Tyler Badie missed practice for a second straight day due to a thumb injury. His status for Sunday's game is in jeopardy; he needs a limited session Friday to have any chance of suiting up. Outside linebacker Jonah Elliss (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) both also were DNPs this week. Hufanga will be ruled out on Friday, and the Broncos anticipate Elliss landing on short-term injured reserve, back at some point later this year. “He’s going to be someone that it’s not season-ending, and so we’re fortunate. So that’ll come out later in the week, but it was better news," head coach Sean Payton said of Elliss on Wednesday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest) and cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) were limited participants; Surtain could be a game-time decision, though Waddle is expected to go. Arizona listed starting safety Budda Baker and running back Jeremiyah Love as DNP for a second consecutive day, as well as safety Andrew Wingard. Cornerback Garrett Williams and defensive lineman Darius Robinson were upgraded to limited. “They give you a couple different looks," Payton noted Wednesday. "They’re in their base defense. They have a penny package. You have to I.D. if they’re in that. Then their pressure package from nickel. They affect the quarterback. I think the other thing that stands out is they’re causing more fumbles in their wins. Their takeaway numbers have been really good, and that’s something you see.” Broncos Get Massive Boost with Return of RB Jonah Coleman Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring The Denver Broncos continued full-scale preparation for Sunday's road game against the Arizona Cardinals, releasing their second injury report ahead of the Week 7 matchup. On it, running back Jonah Coleman (ankle) and cornerback Riley Moss (ribs) were listed as full practice participants for another day, while defensive end Zach Allen was upgraded to full after getting his usual rest day on Wednesday. Cardinals Might Be Down Some Starpower Unfortunately for the home team, the Cardinals are trending toward being at much less than full strength -- at least, according to their Thursday injury report . Baker's absence in particular would be a fortuitous break for a Broncos offense desperately seekin its first true breakout game in 2026. However, Payton knows well enough not to overlook the other 10 players on the Cardinals' defensive side. Surtain, who has missed Denver's last two games with an ankle injury, is unlikely to play Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . The update comes after Surtain returned to practice Wednesday for the first time since suffering a non-contact ankle injury during Denver's 24-14 loss to the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 4. The injury initially raised significant concerns because Surtain went down without contact late in the first half against San Francisco. However, the Broncos subsequently received encouraging news about the injury , with NFL Network's Tom Pelissero reporting that Surtain's Achilles tendon was intact. Surtain missed Denver's 23-17 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers on Oct. 11 and its 17-14 overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks on Oct. 15. The Broncos have relied on their depth in the secondary during his absence. Denver previously elevated two cornerbacks from its practice squad after injuries sidelined Surtain and fellow starter Riley Moss. Moss, who suffered a rib injury against San Francisco, returned against Seattle and played 20 defensive snaps. He practiced fully throughout this week and carries no injury designation for Sunday's game, giving Denver an important boost even if Surtain remains sidelined. Jahdae Barron and Kris Abrams-Draine have also taken on larger responsibilities in the secondary, while Ja'Quan McMillian has continued handling the slot cornerback position. Denver's defensive depth remains under pressure elsewhere. The Broncos enter Sunday's matchup at 4-2 after consecutive victories, while the Cardinals are 2-4.

The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season. The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. away.headline: Packers offensive line stock report: Who steps up as injuries mount?
away.blurb: The move to bring in Laken Tomlinson at left guard has worked out well, and he is the Packers’ top graded offensive lineman this season at 64.2 overall. He has allowed only five quarterback hurries, one hit and zero sacks through four games and also has a 64.5 run block grade. The Green Bay Packers ' offensive line has been the talk of the team all season, and more changes are coming after the top two center options were lost for at least the next four weeks in the space of just a few plays against Detroit. Following a few weeks of continuity, now is an ideal time to assess the status of the individuals comprising the Packers O-line. At tackle, Jordan Morgan is starting to play pretty good football from a pass protection standpoint. He has a snap-weighted PFF pass blocking grade of 76.1 in the last three games and is up to 70.8 for the season. For context, Rasheed Walker had a 68.6 pass block grade for the Packers last year and is down to 65.8 this season with the Panthers . Morgan has allowed five sacks, but was not to blame on multiple of them, including on Sunday against the Lions when it looked like a play was broken or not executed correctly by Jordan Love from the start. There is a big blemish on his record though, which is in run blocking. Walker was never even an average run blocker, with his best grade as a Packer just 56.3, but Morgan is down at 43.4 as we approach the midpoint of the season. While it is not vital for a left tackle to set the tone in the run game, he needs to get closer to average to help get Green Bay’s putrid rushing attack off the ground. Anthony Belton has fared better at right tackle in that regard, but his run block grade is still only 52.2. For a player who was supposed to be a mauler, it has not exactly translated to the NFL level. He struggled somewhat against Detroit, allowing four pressures, but had a snap-weighted pass block grade of 67.1 in the previous three games and did not allow a single pressure in two of the three. Belton is not Zach Bako-Bewele, but he has not been a problem. Tomlinson has simply been solid, which was the hope in bringing him back to a familiar scheme – he played under Kyle Shanahan in San Francisco for five years as well as Mike LaFleur with the Jets – and getting him healthy after some recent troubles in that area. At center, it looks like it will have to be either Williams or Jager Burton for the next month, and although that is certainly cause for concern, the former held up admirably on Sunday after being thrown into the deep end. With Tomlinson seemingly locking down the left guard spot, the most interesting position becomes right guard. Travis Glover was given his shot against Tampa Bay and did well enough to remain in the lineup, but has given up an increasing number of pressures each week, going from one, to two, to three, to five in Detroit. It's been a banged-up unit this year already, and now, the Packers are losing another key starter. While the Panthers' defense isn't one to fear, this Packers team will need to fix this center problem in just a couple of days. Matt LaFleur has dealt with a ton of adversity this season, especially along the offensive line. away.headline: Breaking down Packers' final injury report of Week 7 vs. Lions
away.blurb: The Green Bay Packers listed left guard Aaron Banks, receiver Bo Melton, cornerback Benjamin St-Juste and defensive lineman Jordon Riley as questionable and ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin on the final injury report before facing the Detroit Lions in Week 7 of the 2026 season. LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): Banks got in a second week of practice and could be on the verge of his return to the field for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. If available, the Packers will have to determine if Banks or Laken Tomlinson -- who has started the last three games -- is the best option at left guard on Sunday. WR Bo Melton (back): After missing practices on Wednesday and Thursday, Melton returned in a limited capacity on Friday. The Packers could get by without him at receiver, but he's a core special teamer and a key player for covering kicks and punts. CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring): He didn't play last week after hurting his hamstring against the Bears , but he'll have a chance to return on Sunday after practicing all three days this week. St-Juste is a backup on the perimeter. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): Could he be ready to return? Riley has practiced the last two weeks. The Packers could use another capable player along the defensive front in a matchup against a top running back. LB Zaire Franklin (shin): The defensive's captain injured his shin during Thursday's practice and is out for Sunday. Expect Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper to start at linebacker. A matchup with Jahmyr Gibbs is a tough spot for two backup linebackers. The Lions listed defensive back Brian Branch and center Cade Mays as questionable. Both are coming off injury lists but were full participants at practice on Friday, and both will be expected to play on Sunday. How will the injury situation affect Sunday's NFC North showdown with the Lions? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 7: Defensive lineman Anthony Campbell, cornerback Brandon Cisse, receiver Matthew Golden, quarterback Jordan Love, edge rusher Lukas Van Ness, receiver Christian Watson and receiver Savion Williams do not have a status designation on the final injury report and are good to go for Sunday. Love dealt with back soreness early in the week but was a full participant each of the final two days of practice. Unfortunately, issues that have plagued the team all year, such as injuries, dropped passes, and missed kicks, reared their ugly heads again in Week Seven. Indeed, had the Packers played fundamental and mistake-free football, they would have won the game. After all, the Lions needed a field goal in the closing seconds of the contest in order to win. After the game was over, though, a great deal of criticism was directed at the NFL officials who refereed the game, including by one Packers player who was not able to participate: Micah Parsons . Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons criticizes NFL officials Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) celebrates his sack during the fourth quarter of their game Sunday, September 7, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Multiple players expressed their frustration about bogus roughing the passer calls while Jordan Love was mugged without any flags being thrown. They just want the game called fairly. Parsons, for his part, posted the following message on social media: This particular post is a reference, specifically, to how Brenton Cox was literally pushed into Lions quarterback Jared Goff and whistled for roughing the passer. Over the last several weeks, Green Bay players have been called for this penalty just for putting their hands on an opposing quarterback. At some point, something is going to have to change regarding how the officials are calling Packers games. Even the national media, including Tom Brady, thought the games was terrible in terms of how one-sided the referees were. away.blurb: The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season. “I thought I’d be playing sooner,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I’m just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn’t want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I’m just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing.” Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email GREEN BAY — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs expressed contrition as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked with reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground. “Obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation,” Jacobs said. “Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly.” Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner’s exempt list, which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30 , shortly after charges were filed against him . He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. The Packers (4-2) face the Lions on Sunday in Detroit. Jacobs was arrested May 26 , three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman’s statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently . home.blurb: The Green Bay Packers listed left guard Aaron Banks, receiver Bo Melton, cornerback Benjamin St-Juste and defensive lineman Jordon Riley as questionable and ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin on the final injury report before facing the Detroit Lions in Week 7 of the 2026 season. LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): Banks got in a second week of practice and could be on the verge of his return to the field for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. If available, the Packers will have to determine if Banks or Laken Tomlinson -- who has started the last three games -- is the best option at left guard on Sunday. WR Bo Melton (back): After missing practices on Wednesday and Thursday, Melton returned in a limited capacity on Friday. The Packers could get by without him at receiver, but he's a core special teamer and a key player for covering kicks and punts. CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring): He didn't play last week after hurting his hamstring against the Bears , but he'll have a chance to return on Sunday after practicing all three days this week. St-Juste is a backup on the perimeter. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): Could he be ready to return? Riley has practiced the last two weeks. The Packers could use another capable player along the defensive front in a matchup against a top running back. LB Zaire Franklin (shin): The defensive's captain injured his shin during Thursday's practice and is out for Sunday. Expect Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper to start at linebacker. A matchup with Jahmyr Gibbs is a tough spot for two backup linebackers. The Lions listed defensive back Brian Branch and center Cade Mays as questionable. Both are coming off injury lists but were full participants at practice on Friday, and both will be expected to play on Sunday. How will the injury situation affect Sunday's NFC North showdown with the Lions? Here’s an in-depth breakdown of the Packers ’ final injury report ahead of Week 7: Defensive lineman Anthony Campbell, cornerback Brandon Cisse, receiver Matthew Golden, quarterback Jordan Love, edge rusher Lukas Van Ness, receiver Christian Watson and receiver Savion Williams do not have a status designation on the final injury report and are good to go for Sunday. Love dealt with back soreness early in the week but was a full participant each of the final two days of practice. home.blurb: Josh Jacobs says he is remorseful in first comments since Packers return Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons sounds off on NFL officials following team’s Week 7 loss to Lions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers fell to the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon by the score of 20-17. Unfortunately, issues that have plagued the team all year, such as injuries, dropped passes, and missed kicks, reared their ugly heads again in Week Seven. Indeed, had the Packers played fundamental and mistake-free football, they would have won the game. After all, the Lions needed a field goal in the closing seconds of the contest in order to win. After the game was over, though, a great deal of criticism was directed at the NFL officials who refereed the game, including by one Packers player who was not able to participate: Micah Parsons . Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons criticizes NFL officials Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) celebrates his sack during the fourth quarter of their game Sunday, September 7, 2025 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Green Bay Packers beat the Detroit Lions 27-13. For their part, the Packers players themselves are not making excuses for the loss. That is, they are not at all saying that the reason they lost in Detroit was because of the officials. However, they are frustrated with the confusing calls made against them. Multiple players expressed their frustration about bogus roughing the passer calls while Jordan Love was mugged without any flags being thrown. They just want the game called fairly. Parsons, for his part, posted the following message on social media: This particular post is a reference, specifically, to how Brenton Cox was literally pushed into Lions quarterback Jared Goff and whistled for roughing the passer. Over the last several weeks, Green Bay players have been called for this penalty just for putting their hands on an opposing quarterback. At some point, something is going to have to change regarding how the officials are calling Packers games. Even the national media, including Tom Brady, thought the games was terrible in terms of how one-sided the referees were. home.headline: Detroit Lions injury updates: Dan Campbell shares Monday report
home.blurb: Detroit saw cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. exit with an ankle injury . Star receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown also had an ankle that got checked out on Sunday. Campbell was optimistic about that duo's statuses for the remainder of this week and then heading into Sunday's matchup against the Vikings . "Yeah, I think (Amon-Ra) and Ennis will probably sit Wednesday, but the plan is to get them going Thursday, and I think they'll be fine. They should be good. Now, we'll see when we get there," Campbell said. Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs wisely got down inside the Packers ' 5-yard line after converting a 3rd-and-6. That decision from Gibbs allowed Jake Bates to hit a 22-yard field goal as time expired, eliminating any chance for Jordan Love and the Packers to drive the field or connect on a Hail Mary. But, Gibbs went down awkwardly. Fortunately, Campbell said on Sunday night that everything was good with Gibbs. "Yeah, we got him checked. He should be good. That's that whole is it really worth going down to try to finish the game, or you just go score? Sometimes I question that. I don't know. Maybe we should have just (scored). But, all good. It's a good win," Campbell said. Gibbs finished with 116 rushing yards on 29 carries. St. Brown was the Lions' leading receiver, catching nine passes for 153 yards in the win over the Packers. Kickoff on Sunday is set for 1 p.m. ET between the Lions and Vikings from Ford Field. For more Lions coverage, follow us on X, @TheLionsWire , and give our Facebook page a like .
