home.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Nacua gets back into the race for the triple crown Puka Nacua suffered a calf injury this week in practice, and with Davante Adams on injured reserve, the team could be down their top two pass catchers. Nacua is trending toward playing, and when the cards are stacked against him and the franchise, he has historically always come through. Sunday will be no different as he puts on a statistical display. At least 12 catches for 140 yards and two touchdowns. The Raiders' secondary is suspect, and Nacua always gets his targets. away.headline: Rams Week 7 injury report vs. Raiders: Where Davante Adams, Puka Nacua injuries leave LA offense
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams enter Week 7 against the Las Vegas Raiders without Davante Adams and with another major question surrounding Puka Nacua . Adams is out, while Nacua is questionable with a calf injury after missing Friday’s practice. That combination leaves Los Angeles preparing for two different offensive scenarios: building around an available Nacua or operating without either receiver. Neither offers the flexibility the Rams would have with both in the lineup. The concern extends beyond redistributing targets. Losing receiving options can change defensive coverage, third-down decisions and red-zone planning. With Adams unavailable, Nacua’s status becomes the biggest remaining variable in determining how aggressively Los Angeles can attack through the air. Nacua had no injury listing Wednesday, was limited Thursday and did not participate Friday. That progression raises concern because his involvement decreased before the final report, although it does not establish the injury’s severity or confirm he will miss kickoff. His questionable designation leaves the possibility of playing open. It does not guarantee a normal workload if he is active. The underlying objective would be keeping the offense ahead of the chains. Third-and-long becomes harder when established receiving options are unavailable and defenses can concentrate attention elsewhere. Los Angeles also has uncertainty on defense. Cornerback Trent McDuffie is questionable with a groin injury after missing all three practices. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out with a concussion following three nonparticipation listings. Don't let the home team's offensive struggles fool you, though, as this remains one of the premier clubs in the NFL. Head coach Mike Macdonald's group might have the game's best wide receiver in Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seahawks' defense is in the conversation for being football's most elite unit once again. Kansas City has its work cut out for it in what could be a tough road game, but one thing this year's team has shown is an abundance of grit. Will Sunday Night Football be more of the same? How might today's game unfold? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 7 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: Between the Seahawks’ offensive inconsistencies and the Chiefs’ offensive injuries, this feels like a low-scoring, wire-to-wire affair between two teams with elite elements in some areas and significant questions in others. Ultimately, fitting the narrative of the week perfectly, Kenneth Walker should be the key to this game for both teams. Jordan Foote: Going into Seattle and securing a win is easily the toughest ask of the Chiefs through the first month-and-a-half of the season. The Seahawks' defense, even while banged up, is amazing. On the other side of the ball, however, there's next to no run game. That's had a negative impact on quarterback Sam Darnold, who also isn't sniffing the production he found a season ago. Week 7's tilt could go either way, but I'll side with the offense I believe in much more. Minus wideout Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore , look for this one to be a statement game for one or both of quarterback Patrick Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III in hostile territory. Joshua Schulman: Kenneth Walker is set to return to face the franchise he won a Super Bowl with less than nine months ago, and he'll be looking to make his former team regret letting him walk. He and Jaxon Smith-Njigba headline one of the most exciting Sunday Night Football contests in recent memory. There's a generational quarterback in Patrick Mahomes squaring off against a generational defense that has picked up where it left off a season ago, despite the offense's inconsistencies. Seattle's slow start has actually placed it out of the playoff picture, and a home loss before another prime-time showdown against the Bears would be disastrous. I think the Seahawks understand the importance of this matchup and will take advantage of their 10 days of rest. Given the Chiefs' shaky kicking game and a lack of proven offensive weapons outside of Walker in what should be a low-scoring contest, I think Mike Macdonald and Co. narrowly steal one to hand Kansas City its first loss. Tyler Brown: This one has the look of a defensive rock fight. Seattle’s passing defense ranks first in the NFL, allowing just 141 yards per game, and Kansas City’s defense has held opponents under 20 points in most of its wins. The ingredients are there for a low-scoring grind from start to finish. That said, the Chiefs are the number one offense in the NFL for a reason. Seattle’s defense may be able to slow down Walker or Mahomes, but doing both simultaneously is a different ask entirely. If the run game gets going, the play-action attack opens up. If Mahomes starts finding his receivers, the box opens up for Walker. At some point, one of those two is going to win. On the other side, if Sam Darnold can buy time in the pocket, Smith-Njigba is going to get loose. The Chiefs’ defense just has to make sure that happens once or twice rather than repeatedly. Mahomes has been one of the best quarterbacks against the spread as an underdog in his career, and he finds himself in that spot for the first time in the 2026 season as he and the Chiefs are 2.5-point underdogs against Seattle. The Seahawks are just 3-3 this season and coming off a primetime loss to the Denver Broncos, but their defense remains one of the best in the league in terms of EPA/Play, ranking second through six weeks. Mahomes and the Chiefs are off to a 5-0 start after a win against the Chargers in Week 6, and since they've already had their bye, they're looking to stack wins to take the top seed in the AFC. There are some fun storylines in this matchup, especially with Kenneth Walker III, the Super Bowl MVP from the 2025 season, returning to Seattle for his first game against his former team. Walker is averaging over 6.0 yards per carry this year and has been one of the best weapons in the NFL. This is one of the more even matchups in Week 7, so it’s perfect that it’s a standalone game on Sunday night. Both of these teams have elite defenses and they both are expected to be in the playoff conversation. Does Seattle bounce back, or is this the Chiefs' sixth straight win to open 2026? I've decided to put some of our favorites all into one story ahead of this Week 7 showdown. He has 21 receptions on 29 targets for 206 yards and a touchdown. If he keeps getting that many balls thrown his way, more touchdowns are going to come his way sooner rather than later. He's a great bet to find the end zone at north of 2-1 odds. So far in the 2026 campaign, Walker is averaging 6.3 yards per carry, rushing for 117 or more yards in four of his five appearances. While the Seahawks are allowing just 3.5 yards per carry, it’s hard to fade Walker given all the explosive runs he’s ripped off in the 2026 campaign. While Darnold has some decent passing numbers, he has been a turnover machine. The Kansas City defense is fifth in EPA/Pass this season, and it already has five picks in as many games. Let’s not forget, Darnold threw 12 picks in the 2024 season and 14 in the 2025 season. So, even though he’s become a Super Bowl winning quarterback, the turnovers are still an issue. away.blurb: That is still high, especially given that the Chiefs are hunting wide receiver help, per a report from ESPN's Jeremy Folwer on Monday, October 26, and that Kansas City has around just $2 million in available cap space right now. But mechanisms exist by which the Chiefs can clear up more cap room, and doing so makes sense given their 5-1 start. Reports out of Kansas City indicate that Josh Simmons , a 2025 first-round pick and presumed starting left tackle coming into the season who is now on IR with a back injury, is quickly wearing out his welcome within the organization given a recent blowup between Simmons and head coach Andy Reid during a team meeting session. Chiefs Primed to Pursue Pro Bowl LT Amid Josh Simmons Injury, Poor O-Line Play Unlock the latest Heavy on Chiefs news — direct to your inbox. The Kansas City Chiefs ‘ offensive line is a problem, particularly at the tackle positions, which the Seattle Seahawks defense exposed via a clinical dissection of the Chiefs' front throughout a primetime game that scrubbed some of the shine off the formerly undefeated group. Trading for a starting-level tackle is an incredibly dubious proposition because any teams that have such players are either starting them or holding them as critical swing options who can help an O-line fend off the injury-riddled war of attrition that is every NFL season. But Taylor Decker , the former 10-year starting left tackle of the Detroit Lions , remains a free agent. Why no team added the former Pro Bowler and 140-game starter is a legitimate question, but the answer could be as simple as money. Taylor Decker Perhaps Best Option for Chiefs to Improve Offensive Line Getty Former Detroit Lions left tackle Taylor Decker . Decker asked for, and received, his release from the Lions this offseason. Spotrac projected his market value at $42.5 million over a new two-year contract. At this point in the season, Decker and his camp will presumably be open to a one-year deal, assuming he's still interested in playing. A prorated contract at what appears now to be a meaningfully inflated value projection, the Chiefs could theoretically entice Decker to sign on with a championship-caliber team for the price of around $13 million. Chiefs Tackles Constitute ‘Mess' in Kansas City, as Josh Simmons on IR, at Odds With Team Getty Kansas City Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons. Meanwhile, undrafted rookie Khalil Benson has filled in at the LT position and done so admirably given his lack of NFL experience. But while his run blocking has proven adequate, Benson has struggled meaningfully against opposing pass-rushers and did so again vs. the Seahawks on "Sunday Night Football." "He's done a fine job run blocking, but his pass protection is a mess," Danny Heifetz of The Ringer Fantasy Football Show said of Benson Monday. away.headline: Week 7 Injury Report: Chiefs at Seahawks
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be without running back Zach Charbonnet for another game. Charbonnet, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in the Divisional Round of the playoffs, practiced fully this week, but has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Also ruled out for the Seahawks are linebacker Drake Thomas , who will be out for the second week in a row due to an ankle injury, and linebacker Chazz Surratt , who will be missing a fourth straight game with a calf injury. Among those listed as questionable for the Seahawks is safety Nick Emmanwori , who was a new addition to the injury report on Friday, listed as limited due to a hip. Also questionable are outside linebackers DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and Uchenna Nwosu (hip), both of whom were limited for the second straight day, backup quarterback Drew Lock , who has been limited all week with a right elbow injury, and outside linebacker Connor O'Toole (hamstring), who was limited Friday after not practicing the previous two days. For the Chiefs, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore is out due to a concussion. Left tackle Josh Simmons, who already missed the first five games of the season with a back injury, was placed on injured reserve earlier this week. Also out for Kansas City are receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and running back Brashard Smith (hamstring). For the Chiefs, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and linebacker Cooper Macdonald (knee) are both listed as questionable after being limited in Friday's practice. On a positive note, four players who were limited on Wednesday were upgraded to full participation on Thursday: right guard Anthony Bradford (knee), linebacker Tyrice Knight (oblique), receiver Rashid Shaheed (hip) and guard Beau Stephens (knee). Kansas City's injury report featured only two changes from Wednesday. Running back Brashard Smith was added to the report, listed as limited with a hamstring injury, while left tackle Josh Simmons (back) was removed from the report because he was placed on injured reserve on Thursday. That means that for the second day in a row, right tackle Jaylon Moore (concussion) and receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring, knee) did not practice. Zach Charbonnet , who has a chance to return from the physically unable to perform list this week, was a full participant for the first time since returning to practice earlier this month. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Dallas has dropped two straight games, but Philadelphia enters the NFC East matchup without Jalen Hurts Imagn Images In the Week 7 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Philadelphia Eagles play host to the division rival Dallas Cowboys . Philadelphia has lost four consecutive games after starting the season 2-0, and enters this game ravaged by injuries. Not only is Jalen Hurts out in the wake of blood clots being found in his calf and lungs, but DeVonta Smith , Dontayvion Wicks , Nolan Smith and more will also miss the game, while Saquon Barkley , Landon Dickerson , Jonathan Greenard and Jalyx Hunt are all questionable. Dallas has lost back-to-back games in dispiriting fashion, with its offense sputtering at the worst possible time, combining for 29 points against the Buccaneers and Packers after scoring 30-plus in each of the previous three games. The defense was already under fire early in the season, and now the Cowboys have questions on the side of the ball where they were supposed to be elite. Which of these two teams will stop their losing skid? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Eagles vs. Cowboys live Date: Monday, Oct. 26 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: Lincoln Financial Field (Philadelphia) TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo ( try for free ) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Cowboys -4.5, O/U 43.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Cowboys have the ball Dallas has struggled badly on offense over the last two weeks. The Cowboys did total over 300 yards against both the Buccaneers and the Packers, but those totals are misleading. They were entirely unable to deal with blitzes for essentially all of both contests, and that failure brutally undermined their passing attack. ( Dak Prescott , typically excellent against blitzing defenses, went just 20 of 38 for 194 scoreless yards when confronting extra rushers in those games.) They also ran the ball for a mere 98 yards combined in those two games, despite the fact that star guard Tyler Smith returned to the fold. The struggles came a bit as a surprise considering the Cowboys had previously been cooking offensively, racking up yardage and points through the first four weeks of the season. But both Todd Bowles and Jonathan Gannon came out with a plan that toyed with Dallas' protection rules up front, and the Cowboys found themselves unable to respond. They'll need a significantly better plan on Monday night, but it's notable that the Eagles blitz far less often than the Bucs and Packers did against the Cowboys. The Bucs and Packers sent extra rushers after Prescott on 38.8% of his dropbacks in Weeks 5 and 6, per Tru Media. The Eagles have blitzed just 24.1% of the time so far - the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL . Vic Fangio would have to significantly depart from his modus operandi for Philadelphia to employ a strategy similar to the one that dominated Dallas over the last two weeks. For what it's worth, Philly has blitzed on at least 38% of opponent dropbacks just once since Fangio became the team's defensive coordinator. It would be wildly out of character to break out such a strategy here - but it's one worth pursuing considering Dallas' struggles. Philly checks in 20th in opponents' EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, allowing opponents to complete only 60.4% of passes at an average of 7.0 yards per attempt, but giving up eight touchdown passes against just three interceptions and being helped along by 14 opponent drops - second-most in the league. Cornerbacks Quinyon Mitchell , Riq Woolen and Cooper DeJean are tough to beat, but they have also been asked to cover for too long on some dropbacks because of the Eagles' inability to generate pressure. Philly has gotten a sack, hit or hurry on only 32.9% of opponent dropbacks, and they rank below-average in both average time to pressure and average time to throw. Quarterbacks, in other words, have been fairly comfortable in the pocket. And if you let Prescott get comfortable in the pocket, he can pick you apart with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , among his other targets. The Cowboys seem highly unlikely to find success running the ball, which they haven't done all year. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but he's also averaging only 3.7 yards per carry, down considerably from his 4.8 average last season. The offensive line is not clearing rushing lanes for him, and he's not making anybody miss to make up for it. It's a brutal combination, and with Philly allowing only 4.0 yards per carry, it's not an advantageous one here. When the Eagles have the ball The Eagles enter this game just about as banged up as possible on offense. Quarterback Jalen Hurts is out. His top two receivers, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, are also out. Guard Landon Dickerson remains on injured reserve, though he has been designated to return and listed as questionable for this game. Running back Saquon Barkley is questionable as well, and his top two backups — Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley — are on injured reserve. Without Hurts under center last week, the Eagles operated with a pass-heavy bent. Tanner McKee dropped back to throw 48 times, and while some of that was due to game script and some of it due to Barkley's absence, it's worth noting that he had previously made two Week 18 starts and dropped back to pass an average of 44 times in those games as well. The Eagles can't use the quarterback run game with McKee under center like they can with Hurts, and the rest of their run-game efficiency is likely to suffer as a result of not presenting that threat to the defense. It's somewhat reasonable to expect them to be pass-heavier than we're used to here. That may not be the case if Barkley returns to the lineup, but it is at least somewhat difficult to parse what the Eagles would prefer to do in that situation. Barkley has actually averaged 5.5 yards per carry in each of the two games he's made it through healthy this season. The problem is that the rest of the backs have been extremely inefficient in his absence and he wasn't efficient before leaving the other two games due to injury, either. He fully practiced on Friday for the first time since his hamstring injury, but the team may not want to load him up with too many touches in his first game back in the fold. Every team that is humanly capable of running the football (i.e., not the Texans or Packers) has done so at will against the Cowboys this season, with Dallas' other five opponents each piling up at least 165 yards on the ground. Opponents have clipped the Cowboys for 4.7 yards per carry, with running backs and quarterbacks alike able to find considerable room to run against a disappointingly friendly Dallas front. If the Eagles can get Barkley (or Dameon Pierce ) going early, they might be able to lean on the Cowboys and prevent the game from turning into the kind of track meet that Dallas' offense would prefer. Opponents have also generally been able to throw all over the Cowboys, though it will obviously be difficult for the Eagles to do so while down their top two receivers and multiple of their expected starting offensive linemen. It'll be Makai Lemon , Darius Cooper and Dallas Goedert as McKee's top targets here. It'll be interesting to see if the Cowboys send Joey Porter Jr . to follow one of Cooper (who plays outside) or Lemon (usually in the slot, where he would match up more often with Caleb Downs ), as well as how they align their secondary now that Cobie Durant is set to return and potentially push the struggling (to say it kindly) Daron Bland to the bench. If the Cowboys can put any semblance of pressure on McKee, he could struggle badly. He's just 16 of 45 for 179 scoreless yards in his career when under duress, with a 15.1% sack rate as well. The Cowboys don't rush the passer particularly well, but with the current state of Philly's offensive line, that could change on Monday night. I just don't think the Cowboys should be favored by more than a field goal against anybody right now, given how they're playing on both sides of the ball. I'll take Dallas to win given the state of the Eagles' offense, but I can't see the Cowboys blowing anyone out in their current state. It has been a brutally tough season for both teams, with Philly and Dallas both sitting at 2-4 entering Week 7. The Cowboys and Eagles were viewed as the best teams in the division going into the season, yet they are both trailing the New York Giants, who look like the least dysfunctional team in the NFC East after seven weeks. But all that matters right now is what happens on Monday night. And, speaking of Monday night, here's a look at who the majority of experts from different media outlets are picking between the Cowboys and Eagles. After all, the Eagles won't have Jalen Hurts and are instead starting Tanner McKee, and even their best wide receiver, Dontayvion Wicks and DeVonta Smith, are out . Philly is going to be short-handed on defense, also, with Nolan Smith, who is their sacks leader, ruled out, and then there's also Jonathan Greenard, who is questionable to play . However, after what we've witnessed over the last six weeks, there are no guarantees with this lackluster Cowboys team, and especially because of the putrid defense . There is hope yet, though, as the defense will welcome back Cobie Durant, who was the Cowboys' best corner during the offseason, and DeMarvion Overshown. The returns of those two players , combined with the Eagles' key injuries on offense, should be enough for the Cowboys to have a bounce-back showing on defense and keep Philly in check. away.headline: Cowboys-Eagles final injury update has 7 ruled out including Smith
away.blurb: Running back Saquon Barkley is on track to appear for the first time since leaving the Week 4 game early, and should bring a huge boost to a running game that has floundered the last three weeks. Hopefully ready to meet him in the hole is linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who hasn't seen action since Week 1 for the Cowboys. The Cowboys also expect CB Cobie Durant to return to action, and he hasn't played since Week 2. Those are two big additions for Dallas. Things are trending right for several other Cowboys, though they aren't quite ready to return to action. The Cowboys opened the 21-day practice window for LB Marist Liufau and safety PJ Locke. Both were expected to be key reserves this year and still could be activated before Monday's game, with corresponding roster moves. Starting safety Jalen Thompson can have his window opened next week. Meanwhile, Dallas did rule out WR/KR Kavontae Turpin (ribs) and LB Dee Winters (calf), along with OT Drew Shelton. McKee won't have his top two receivers as both DeVonta Smith and Dontarin Wycks have been ruled out. Barkley is one of seven listed as questionable, along with OF Landon Dickerson and edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who is expected to be a game-time decision . Entering their Week 7 Monday Night Football matchup, the teams sport identical 2-4 records after six games , with injuries the underlying factor of both club's malaise. Dallas, implementing a new defense under first-year coordinator Christian Parker, has seen their back-seven progressively decimated week by week, undermining his attempt to get his footing as a scheme designer and playcaller. The Eagles have just lost body after body throughout their roster, losing key contributors to the offense. Are the clubs trending in opposite directions despite losing streaks for both ? Injury wise, Dallas is starting to get some contributors back, with the question being about whether they can actually make a difference or is Parker's scheme a bad one. The Eagles are trending down, still, though they will get a big boost from one returning member. For Philly, the injury discussion has centered around QB Jalen Hurts and the controversy over his blood clot diagnosis . Regardless of the inner workings there, he's been moved to IR and is done for the year, opening the door for Tanner McKee to get the start and raising the possibility if he flounders, the Eagles could turn to Joe Milton III at QB. Philly snatched him off of Dallas' practice squad last week . Here's a look at the complete injury report from Saturday.

home.headline: Eagles’ Britain Covey ruled out for the rest of MNF with knee injury
home.blurb: Taking to social media to update fans on the returner’s status after suffering a knee injury in the first quarter, Covey has officially been ruled out for the remainder of the contest , with recent practice squad signee Elijah Mitchell appearing in his first game since 2025, taking over on the team’s second kick return of the contest. Initially joining the Birds as a 24-year-old undrafted rookie out of Utah, Covey has exclusively played for Philly as a pro, temporarily leaving the team in May of 2025 to sign with the Los Angeles Rams, only to return to the Eagles’ practice squad in August following his release. While he’s never been targeted more than eight times in a season as a wide receiver, his production as a kick and punt returner has kept him in the mix through multiple Super Bowl runs, one he won – on injured reserve – and one he lost. With Covey out, it would appear Mitchell will be in charge of return duties in a game where no team punted at the midway point of the second quarter, taking his first chance 16 yards before a touchback prevented a second return. With no kick returns on his career , largely with the San Francisco 49ers, Mitchell will have a regular baptism by fire in his first game of the 2026 season. As the Philadelphia Eagles look to end their four-game losing streak on Monday Night Football against their arch-divisional rivals, the Dallas Cowboys, they will have to do so without one of their key special teams players: Britain Covey.
